functions.name: Date_ToDayIndex

findings.title: setup and inventory
findings.body:
Track: B (setup, milestone 1).

### Pinned exe

- `eFootball-PES-2021/eFootball PES 2021/PES2021.exe`, 458,739,200 bytes, SHA-256 `58964c5a56dd5c4be2aa54a91444ed4fae61e899a1983f088bf5110167945ad9`. **confirmed** (guide section 5).
- pesrecomp's `config/versions/cpy-1.07.json` and `out/ghidra/import_report.json` record the same SHA-256. Its static artifacts (catalogue, Ghidra project, feature files) were built from this exe. **confirmed** (hash string match in both files).

### Open: version label conflict

- Guide section 5 calls this exe v1.01, unpatched (matches all 42 "old" bytes of Sider's `pes2021.1.01.00.cmp`).
- pesrecomp labels the same hash "CPY release, 1.07.0x".
- The hash is the same, so every address is unaffected. Only the label differs. Unresolved. Next check: read the PE version resource of the exe.

### Not available

- FL_2026.exe and PES2020.exe are not on this machine and cannot be obtained for now. Milestone 3 (FootballLife address carry-over through `tools/version_join.py`) and the PES 2020 constants cross-check are blocked. Neither blocks section 12, the referee pilot, or Track C.
- PS4 eboot already exists at pesrecomp `data/ps4/eboot.bin` (79.2 MB). Its patch version is not yet checked.

### pesrecomp reuse (guide section 13)

pesrecomp lives at `/Users/[redacted]/Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace/pesrecomp`. Its `.venv` works (capstone 5.0.7, unicorn). Tools to reuse: `verify_strings.py`, `verify_impdata_addr.py`, `verify_aoba.py`, `verify_census.py`, `aoba_xref.py`, `aoba_symbols.py`, `extra_funcs.py`, `close_catalog.py`, `call_gap.py`, `version_join.py`, `engine_match.py`, `ghidra_query.py`, `hw_*.py`, `recon_ab.py`, `recon_golden.py`.

Caveats:

- `analysis/catalog_cpy-1.07.json` claims 233,322 functions. **probable** (README claim, not re-measured here).
- The Ghidra import ran with ASCII Strings, Decompiler Switch Analysis and Function ID missing (transaction errors in `import_report.json`). String xrefs and jump tables from Ghidra are incomplete.
- `build/`, `out/` and `local/` (about 137 GB) are frozen. Do not extend.

findings.title: section 12 open rows (static)
findings.body:
Track: B, milestone 1. Script: `src/tools/check_sec12.py`, follow-up `src/tools/probe_sec12_followup.py`. Log: `logs/2026-11-02-sec12.log` (local only). The exe hash was checked as pinned at the start of the run.

Acceptance criteria were set before running: (a) each wiki string has a rip-relative reference at or next to the wiki address, (b) each stub is a 5-byte `jmp` into `.impdata` whose target decodes as an ordinary function ending in `ret`, (c) the version resource names the version.

### a. Debug strings: PASS, 4 of 4

| String | Wiki address | Reference | Literal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kick Action Decided | `0x14210DDD2` | `lea rdx` at `0x14210DDC5` (-13) | `0x142BEE870` |
| SetLyaer | `0x1406F0BE4` | `lea rdx` at `0x1406F0BDD`, ends at the wiki address | `0x1425DE770` |
| ragdoll_Ayashii | `0x1406E6064` | `lea rdx` at `0x1406E6067` (+3) | `0x1425DEAB0` |
| Change ControlMode | `0x1408A93B0` | `lea rdx` at `0x1408A93A9`; the wiki address is `call 0x1405CE4E0` (debug print) | `0x14260CCB0` "[Command] Change ControlMode by gage use..." |

The first pass marked "Change ControlMode" FAIL. That was my literal search matching 10 bytes inside the string; it was not a mismatch in the exe. Wiki addresses sit within 13 bytes of the referencing instruction, not exactly on it. **confirmed** (static).

### b. Relocated stubs: PASS, 2 of 2

- `ScoreToSeverity` `0x1405B6800`: `jmp 0x143F71690`, 5 bytes. The target is in `.impdata` and is a `.pdata` start. 14 instructions, `push rbx` prologue, ends in `ret`. It calls `0x1405B82E0` (the `GetFoulThresholds` stub). **confirmed** (static shape). The names stay **probable** (Aoba).
- `GetFoulThresholds` `0x1405B82E0`: `jmp 0x143FA8760`, 5 bytes. The target is in `.impdata` and is a `.pdata` start (extent ends `0x143FA8834`). 54 instructions, standard save-registers prologue, ends in `ret` at `0x143FA8833`. **confirmed** (static shape).
- Corroboration for the Aoba chain: `GetFoulThresholds` calls `0x140A48A10` and `0x140A48A30` (Aoba's `GetPlayerData` and `GetTeamData`), plus `0x1405B6870` and `0x140A72E70` (unnamed).

### New: threshold word in GetFoulThresholds

Branch at `0x143FA8800` (`jae`) picks one of two 16-bit values written to `[rdi]`:

- taken: immediate `0x5028`, so the bytes are 40, 80;
- not taken: `word [0x1482B3DC8] ^ 0x50FC`. The raw file value is `0x00C0`, which decodes to `0x503C`, so the bytes are 60, 80.

40/80 matches the wiki's T1=40, T2=80. **probable**: the instruction semantics are confirmed statically, but the file value at `0x1482B3DC8` is not checked at run time, and the branch condition is not yet understood. `0x1482B3DC8` sits next to the known XOR constant at `0x1482B3DC4` (raw `0xC749DAD1`, re-read today). Next check: hit-count and value probe on `0x143FA8810` vs `0x143FA8816` during fouls (section 9.4, needs the VM).

### c. Version label: resolved

The PE version resource says FileVersion `1.1.0.0`, ProductVersion `1.1.0.0`, ProductName "eFootball PES 2021". That agrees with the guide's "1.01". pesrecomp's "1.07.0x" label is not supported by the exe; it is probably a release-group label. **confirmed** for the resource strings.

### Still open in section 12

- Position-compatibility bytes at `0x142613D20`: no reference to compare against. Stays open.

Section 12 is now 7 of 8 rows passing. None failed, so the build does not need re-pinning.

findings.title: FootballLife addresses hold in my exe without FL_2026.exe
findings.body:
Track: B, milestone 3 (partial: answers open question 3 without the FL exe). Script: `src/tools/check_fl_carry.py`. Log: `logs/2026-11-02-fl-carry.log`.

Acceptance criteria were set before running: instruction text quoted by FootballLife must decode at exactly that address in my exe, and FL addresses must hit my catalogued starts far above a shifted control.

- 5 of 5 quoted instructions match at the exact address: `0x1414B6F72` `mov edx,0x1877068`; `0x141264659` `cmp eax,0xe80` and `0x141264B51` `mov r12d,0x26000001` (the original bytes the fl26reg64 patch replaces); `0x1414C9CC0` `and dword [rcx+0x304],0x3fffffff`; `0x14134E910` `cmp eax,0x7d0` right after `call 0x1414c9890`.
- 98 of 140 distinct FL `.trace` addresses are my catalogued function starts. Control: the same addresses + 0x40 give 5. Most of the other 42 are documented as interior sites, not starts.
- Correction kept: the first run showed 2/5. That was three errors on my side, not in the exe. I paired the 0x141264659 address with the 0x141264B51 bytes, read row 50's call as the instruction at the address (it is the one before), and included `0x140A6C54A`, which comes from Sider's custom-events example (`RE-INVENTORY.md` line 324), not from FootballLife. It was dropped.

Reading: FL_2026.exe's `.trace` appears to be my exe (FileVersion 1.1.0.0) plus FootballLife's byte patches and added sections. That is consistent with its file being 171,520 bytes larger. **probable**: shown for 5 instructions and 98 function starts, not for the whole section. Consequence: FootballLife addresses can be carried over one by one with a local check (start in catalogue, or quoted bytes match). They are not yet applied in the DB.

findings.title: referee batch 1 named and spot-checked
findings.body:
Track: B, toward milestone 6. pes-namer named 17 functions from the Ghidra output, all `probable` or `guess`, source `ai`. Rows: `db/seeds/referee1.tsv` (tracked); `seed_db.py` now applies `db/seeds/*.tsv` over the Aoba names and keeps the Aoba name in `seeds`. pes-skeptic checked 3 of 17 rows (18%) against raw disassembly.

Skeptic results:

- **GetFoulThresholds** (`0x1405B82E0` -> `0x143FA8760`): holds. `bt eax,0xb` at `0x143FA87FC` tests bit 11 of the `0x140A72E70` result. Bit clear writes `0x5028` (T1 40, T2 80). Bit set writes `word[0x1482B3DC8]^0x50FC`, which is 60, 80 from the file value. `mov byte [rdi+2],0x6e` at `0x143FA87F8` is unconditional, so **T3 = 110 in both cases**. This answers the branch question from the earlier entry. The 60 stays **probable** until the word is read at run time.
- **ScoreToSeverity** (`0x1405B6800` -> `0x143F71690`): holds, and the exact semantics are pinned. The score and thresholds are unsigned bytes. score < T1 gives 0. score < T2 gives 1, or 2 when score > T1 + ((T2-T1) >> 1); the comparison is strict and the midpoint is floored. score < T3 gives 3, otherwise 4. With 40/80/110: 39 gives 0, 40 to 60 give 1, 61 to 79 give 2, 80 to 109 give 3, 110 and above give 4. **probable** (static, instruction-level).
- **ClassifyFoulZone** (`0x140A72E70`): mechanics hold. In the band |x| > `p[+0x18]` and |z| < `p[+0x1c]` (both strict), the result is 0x800 when teamDir*x > 0, else 0x400. **Not settled statically:** whether 0x800 means the box the team attacks or its own box. So "60/80 inside the attacked box" remains unproven.
- Severity labels (3 = yellow, 4 = red) are **guess**; no string anchors them.
- Aoba names the batch judges wrong or unsupported (**guess**): `GetAdjustedPosition` (looks like the foul position), `FoulEventRouter` (a general match-event handler), `CardEscalation`, `ParallelFoulTracker`, `CardTrackerDispatch`.

Next runtime check (VM, guide 9.4): one value probe at `0x143FA87F8`. Capture the classify result in `eax`, `[team+0x254]` and the x float at `[rsp+0x20]`, read the word at `0x1482B3DC8` at run time, and count hits at `0x143FA8810` vs `0x143FA8816` over a match.

findings.body:
Track: C (shared with B), tier `exact`, port_status: reimplemented, **not verified** against the running game. Written by pes-porter.

- `src/game/referee/foul_severity.{h,cpp}`: `score_to_severity` and `foul_thresholds` in namespace `pes::referee`. The {40,80,110} and {60,80,110} threshold sets are data in `RefereeRules`, not logic. The zone flag is named neutrally because which box it means is unsettled. No platform headers and no raw addresses (grep-checked).
- Static library `pes_game` (no SDL), test `tests/game/foul_severity_test.cpp` under CTest: a full 0..255 sweep, boundaries, the zone set, and a degenerate t1 == t2 case. `ctest`: 1/1 pass.
- Contract check: changing the midpoint test from `>` to `>=` makes the test fail with 3 failures (scores 60 and 70). Restored, rebuilt, pass. During this a stale object first made the restored build look failing; a touch and rebuild fixed it. Lesson: after a mutation check, force a rebuild of the restored file.
- Limit: the expected values come from the same static reading as the code. They guard the transcription, not the reading. Verification needs recorded cases from the PC game (guide 9.4, VM).

findings.title: iOS build not attempted (blocked)
findings.body:
Track: C, milestone 2 (iPad half). Xcode 16.4, the iOS 18.5 SDK and simulator, and 2 code-signing identities are present. `CMakeLists.txt` has an iOS branch that fetches SDL3 `release-3.4.18` (the brew version) and builds it statically. Running it was refused by the auto-mode permission check, because the build downloads and compiles code from GitHub. It needs the owner's approval. Command to run by hand:

    cmake -B build-ios-sim -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=iOS -DCMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT=iphonesimulator -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 && cmake --build build-ios-sim -j2 --target pes_host

The iOS branch is unbuilt and **unverified**.

findings.title: C++ CPK reader matches the pes-file-tools oracle
findings.body:
Track: A/C, milestone 4 (first part). Written by pes-porter; the CRILAYLA real-data check was added by the main session.

- `src/engine/formats/cpk/` (static lib `pes_engine`, no SDL): `Archive::open`, `entries()`, `extract()`. Reads only the header, TOC and requested entry, and never the whole archive. Every offset and size is bounds-checked; tables are capped at 256 MiB; CRILAYLA output is capped. Format note in my own words: `docs/formats/cpk.md`. pes-file-tools has no licence, so its code was read and run as an oracle, not copied.
- Oracle: pes-file-tools' own Python reader, run `python3 -I -B` from a scratch dir. Scripts: `src/tools/oracles/`.
- Results (`PES_DATA` set; `ctest`: 3/3 pass; without `PES_DATA` the golden test is skipped):
  - Uncompressed: 66 entries in dt42_all, dt18_all, dt17_x64 and dt10_x64 match entry for entry (listing hash plus a hash per file). **confirmed** against the oracle.
  - CRILAYLA: the small archives have no compressed entries. A TOC-only scan found compressed entries in `dt00_x64` (1 of 496: `movie/fade/settings.json`, 548 to 1,614 bytes) and `dt14_all` (14,671 of 14,672, `.dds` symbols). Both checked entries match the oracle. A corrupted golden hash makes the test exit 1. **confirmed** for these 2 entries.
- PES detail: file offsets count from `TocOffset` (0x800), not `ContentOffset` (0x1000). **probable** (holds on all archives tested).
- Not supported: ITOC-only and ETOC-only archives. Column types other than 0, 2, 4, 6 and 10 are a guess.
- Housekeeping: the porter's first oracle run wrote `__pycache__` into `pes-file-tools-master`. It was removed, and no `.pyc` files remain. Always use `-B`.

findings.title: C++ ftex reader matches the oracle on 7 real textures
findings.body:
Track: A/C, milestone 4 (second part). Written by pes-porter; re-run and checked by the main session (`ctest` 5/5 with `PES_DATA`, layering grep clean, no `.pyc` in third-party).

- `src/engine/formats/ftex/` (in `pes_engine`, links the system zlib from the macOS SDK; nothing downloaded): `parse()`, `to_dds()`, own `PixelFormat` enum. Bounds-checked; each mip level is capped at 256 MiB, the whole texture at 512 MiB. Format note: `docs/formats/ftex.md`. Oracle: `src/tools/oracles/ftex_oracle.py` (pes-file-tools `ftexToDds`).
- 7 of 7 real entries match the oracle (DDS SHA-256 plus format, width, height, mips): badges (BC3, BC7), a collar (BC3), boots (BC5 normal map, BC1), and two kit textures from `dt34_g4.cpk`: `Asset/model/character/uniform/texture/#windx11/u0014p2_name_ex.ftex` (BC7 1024x512, 9 mips) and `u0133g1_chest.ftex` (BC7 1024x128). A corrupted golden hash fails the test. **confirmed** for the chunked-zlib BC1/BC3/BC5/BC7 2D path on these entries.
- Seen in the data: formats BC1, BC3, BC5 and BC7 (ids 2, 4, 9, 11), versions 2.03 and 2.04, ftexs count always 0.
- Unverified: other format ids, cube maps, volumes, `.ftexs` side files (rejected with an error), PS4 tiling, colour-space bits.
- Milestone 4 still needs the VFS mount and the texture on screen. Apple-silicon Metal supports BC formats on macOS; iPad needs a check or a CPU decode.

findings.title: milestone 4 met on macOS (kit texture on screen through my VFS)
findings.body:
Track: C (with A). Written by pes-porter; the visual check was done by the main session.

- `src/engine/vfs/`: `Vfs::mount_dir` reads only the TOCs of every `*.cpk` in a directory, in sorted filename order. Real `Data/`: 29 archives, 80,516 unique paths, 121 duplicate paths, 0 failed. Peak RSS for the full mount is 44.9 MB. Duplicate rule "last mounted wins" is a **guess**: every duplicate is a lower-numbered archive overridden by a higher one, which fits but does not prove it. `vfs_unit` test covers lookup, a missing path and override order.
- Host: `pes_host --data <Data> --show <vfs path> [--snapshot /tmp/x.bmp]` reads an ftex through the VFS, uploads mip 0 as a native BC texture (Metal on Apple silicon supports BC7), and blits it scaled to fit. No custom shaders. Error exits: 1 when the load fails, 2 when `--data` is missing, 3 when the format is unsupported.
- Evidence: `a0150g1.ftex` (2048x2048 BC7, from `dt34_g4.cpk`) shows a complete kit UV layout in plausible colours: white body, sponsor, crest, maker logo, sleeve badges. I viewed it from the snapshot (`/tmp`, not in the repo). The first test texture, `u0014p2_name_ex.ftex`, turned out to be an extended-letter glyph sheet (ö, ü), not a kit. **confirmed** for macOS, milestone 4 wording ("VFS mounts my CPKs; a C++ ftex reader shows a kit texture").
- Limits: the snapshot is a second render into an offscreen texture, not a swapchain readback. sRGB versus linear handling is unchecked. Only mip 0 is uploaded. iPad is not done (see the iOS entry).
- `ctest` 6/6 pass with `PES_DATA`.

findings.title: parser hardening after review
findings.body:
Track: C. cavecrew-reviewer reviewed the CPK, ftex and VFS readers (1 red, 10 yellow). I checked the cited lines before acting. Fixed by pes-porter, each with a regression test that failed on the old code (except row_len==0, which the old code already rejected; that test is kept as a guard):

- UTF table: 64 MiB cap on copied strings and blobs, at most 1<<20 rows and 1<<22 cells, per-row columns with row_len 0 rejected.
- CRILAYLA: 256 MiB output cap checked before allocation.
- ftex: a zlib chunk must produce exactly its declared size; per-record ftexs byte must be 0. **New format fact:** a declared chunk size of 0 means 65536 (u16 wrap). The real files use 64 KiB chunks, not the 16 KiB the earlier note said. Found because the golden test failed under the stricter check. **confirmed** on the 7 golden entries.
- VFS: `mount_dir` no longer aborts on filesystem errors and records failures per file; `mount` keeps the archive and label lists in step.
- CPK names with `..`, empty segments or a leading `/` are rejected at open.
- Documented as not thread-safe: `Archive::extract`, `Vfs::read`.
- Left as documented risk: the entry-offset base heuristic (`TocOffset` vs `ContentOffset`).

Gate (re-run by the main session): `ctest` 6/6 with `PES_DATA`; real mount still shows 29 archives, 80,516 files, 0 failed; kit snapshot checksum matches the earlier run.

findings.title: pesdb tables load through my VFS (milestone 8, format level)
findings.body:
Track: A/C. Written by pes-porter; re-run by the main session (`ctest` 8/8 with `PES_DATA`; golden files hold counts and hashes only).

- **Wrapper:** each `common/etc/pesdb/*.bin` starts with `ff 10 81 "WESYS"`, then u32 compressed size, u32 uncompressed size, then a zlib stream. No encryption. `Player.bin`: 1,227,668 + 16 = file size, inflating to 5,547,984 = 17,782 x 312. **confirmed** (exact arithmetic; oracle match). The first 3 bytes are unexplained.
- `src/engine/formats/pesdb/`: Player, Team, Competition, CompetitionEntry, CompetitionKind. Rows on this install: 17,782 / 663 / 91 / 1,291 / 9. dt00 and dt10 hold identical copies of these tables. RE-INVENTORY's 27,927 players and 743 teams are Football Life's modded database, not this install.
- Oracle: FootballLife `tools/pesdb.py` (MIT, credited in `CREDITS.md`). Counts and canonical-dump hashes match on all 5 tables. Caveat: FL has no Player parser, so the Player comparison checks my C++ against FL's *documented* bit layout, not against the game.
- Confidence: wrapper, player id and names, and kind ids are **confirmed**; the six player bit fields, team id/name, and competition and entry fields are **probable** (FL layout); the team manager dword, competition `parent` and kind bytes 1 to 3 are **guess**. Unknown bytes stay raw.
- Peak RSS for the full mount plus loading all five tables: 56.2 MB.
- Not done: Coach, Stadium, Regulation and the other tables; the other ~90 player ability fields; `src/game` types; host use. Milestone 8 wording ("into my own types") is met only at format-record level.

findings.title: competition subsystem batch 1 (FootballLife seeds, checked on my exe)
findings.body:
Track: B, toward the second pilot (guide 9.6). Ghidra batch: 15 functions in about 10 s (`private-reference/pc/ghidra/competition1/`). pes-namer named them from FL's descriptions plus my decompile; 16 rows (including the progression switch) are in `db/seeds/competition1.tsv`. pes-skeptic checked 3 claims (20%) at instruction level. All held.

- **The door, `0x1413AC170` `Competition_Season_TryEnterCompetition`:** it takes a **u16 regulation id**, matched against record+0 in the null-returning lookup `0x1414BC860`, not a bare competition id as FL describes. It refuses unless bit 8 of `[rec+0x304]` is set. It dispatches on dword `[rec+0x84]`: 1 is a league (`0x1413F36C0`, with an extra flag from `0x141546A40`), 3 a knockout (`0x1413F49F0`), 4 goes to `0x1413F63E0`; 2, 5 and 6 succeed without fixtures; anything else returns 0. On success it calls `0x1413AC310`. **probable**. Record+0 and the dword at record+0x80 (set from a signed byte) are distinct fields. That record+0 packs the competition in its low byte and a group in its high bits is **not shown**.
- **Progression switch `0x141345CC0`:** handles ids 2..175 through a 174-byte table at `0x141345F74` and 11 jump-table entries at `0x141345F48`; ids outside the range go to the default. Handled ids: {2}, {3,9,15,34,44,47,77}, {4}, {5}, {8}, {10,16}, {41,104}, {79,80,82}, {134,135,136,147,148,152-156,172,175}, {168,169}. The other 118 ids are a no-op. **probable** (decoded twice independently). This is FL's "case table over 2..175". It is a progression dispatch, not the list of ids that register.
- **Regulation table `0x1414BB000` `GetOrBlank`:** array at edit+0xC12E9C, stride 0x314, keyed by the u16 at +0. Count at edit+0xD0BCF4. Id 0xFFFF or a miss returns the blank record at edit+0xD0B77C, never null. A linear mode (edit+0x183789C == 2) is capped at 300 records; otherwise it uses a lower_bound at `0x1414B7FE0`. **probable**. The sort order is not confirmed statically.
- **Not found:** the compiled-in list of competition ids that register each season (FL's "55 ids"). Its builder is driver `0x141314FC0` (20-byte event entries). A 112-row table at `0x1434EECC0` ({u16 id, u16 0, u32 slot, u32 kind}) is read just before `register_all`; its role is a **guess**.
- Regulation runtime fields from the parser (`private-reference/pc/naming/competition1-namer.md`) agree with RE-INVENTORY 2.2. **probable**.
- Catalogue note: some functions are split into small `.trace` chunks in the pesrecomp catalogue (for example, `0x141343BF0` has size 6). Sizes in `functions` are not function lengths.

Next runtime check (VM): dump the u16 at +0 and the dword at +0x80 for the first 20 regulation records at edit+0xC12E9C. That settles the sort order and the id layout. Next static step: decode `0x141314FC0` and `0x141315FD0` to find the include list.

findings.title: the "55-id include list" is not a literal in the exe (bounded search)
findings.body:
Track: B. FL (`research-findings.md` ~line 12553) says the season builder `0x1413156E0` runs at creation with a fixed include list of 55 ids, "static in the exe", containing `... 67 68 76 93 94 96 97 98 119 ... 162 ...`.

- Searched `.rdata`, `.data` and `.trace` for the run 67, 68, 76, 93, 94, 96, 97, 98 as consecutive u8, u16 and u32: **no hit**.
- Ghidra decompiles of the driver `0x141314FC0` and its neighbours `0x141315FD0`, `0x141362480`, `0x141367290`, `0x141348210` and `0x141367010` contain none of those ids as immediates. The driver walks a runtime vector of 20-byte entries.
- Reading: the list is probably assembled at run time from data (event or calendar entries), not compiled in as a table. This contradicts FL's "static in the exe". **guess**: the search is bounded to contiguous runs and to those six functions. Other encodings (deltas, bitsets, non-consecutive order) are not excluded.
- Runtime check (VM): break at `0x1413156E0` at career creation and dump the include vector (third argument) plus the source of the 20-byte entries.

findings.title: naming as we go (Track B tooling)
findings.body:
- Seeds now cover data as well as functions. New tables `data` (28 rows: 2 constants, 4 tables, 4 strings, 18 instruction sites) and `fields` (11 rows: `EditData` and `RegulationRecord` offsets) in `db/functions.sqlite`, from `db/seeds/data/` and `db/seeds/structs/`. 7 functions from earlier entries were named in `db/seeds/findings1.tsv` (3 `guess`, 4 `probable`, none reviewed by pes-skeptic yet). 5 decompiled neighbours whose role is unknown, the `.pdata` extent end and the dropped Sider address are listed in `db/seeds/skip/findings1.tsv`.
- `src/tools/check_names.py` (ctest `names_cover_findings`): 59 addresses cited here, 59 covered. Mutation check: deleting the `0x1482B3DC8` data row gives exit 1 naming that address; a seed file newer than the db gives exit 1 (stale).
- `src/tools/ghidra_apply_names.py` writes the names into `private-reference/pc/ghidra-project` (APFS clone of pesrecomp's project, which stays untouched): 103 functions, 4 relocated bodies (`<name>_body`), 10 labels, 18 site EOL comments; peak RSS 465 MB. Check: the decompile of `0x1413AC170` now shows `Competition_RegulationTable_Find`, `Competition_FixtureBuilder_BuildLeague` and `Competition_Regulation_GetLeagueFixtureFlag`; the body `0x143FA8760` shows `Referee_Pitch_ClassifyFoulZone` and `Referee_ZoneThresholds_Xored`. Site comments are not in ghidra_query's JSON output, so they were not checked that way.
- Not applied to Ghidra: struct fields (no types created). Names deleted from the db stay in the Ghidra copy until it is re-cloned.

findings.title: future-proofing (Track B tooling)
findings.body:
- Signatures: `src/tools/sigs.py make` writes `db/sigs.tsv` and the `sig` columns. It gives 115 unique signatures (functions from their entry, or from the `.impdata` body for stubs; sites from the site). Relative branches, RIP-relative displacements and image-address immediates are masked. Each signature grows until it matches exactly once in `.trace` + `.impdata`. 6 have no unique prefix within 96 bytes: `Debug_PrintfStub`, the `ret` site, and 4 functions with duplicate bodies (`RegisterSituationEnums`, `Competition_Season_RegisterAll`, `Competition_Regulation_GetRoundIndex`, `WriteHumanControllerFlags`). Check: `sigs.py find` on the pinned exe finds 115 of 115 once, each at its own address. Mutation: flipping one byte at `0x140423000` in a cloned exe reports `MatchControlUpdate` as missing; the other 114 are still found.
- `src/tools/rebuild_names.sh` runs `seed_db`, `classify_relocated`, `sigs make`, `ghidra_apply_names` and `check_names` in order (51 s end to end).
- Port tracking: named functions are `named`. `db/seeds/ports/referee.tsv` marks `ScoreToSeverity` and `GetFoulThresholds` as `reimplemented`, `exact`, in `src/game/referee/foul_severity.cpp` (static decode only, not compared with the game). Counts: named 101, reimplemented 2.
- `TOOLCHAIN.md` (from `src/tools/toolchain.sh`): Ghidra 12.1.2, pyghidra 3.1.0, capstone 5.0.7, SDL3 3.4.18 (linked headers; brew also keeps 3.4.16 installed), CMake 4.4.3, Apple clang 17.0.0.
- `tests/behaviour/probes.tsv`: VM probes P1 to P4 (P1b is a companion of P1), all as entry/exit captures (guide 9.2 rule 4). P1 reads the threshold output bytes at exit through the saved second argument (`mov rdi,rdx` at `0x143FA877B`), so no mid-function patch is needed. `check_names.py` now also fails when a probe hook has no signature. Mutation: renaming P2's hook gives exit 1.
- pes-namer is told to read the existing names from the db and the named Ghidra copy, and to propose data and struct rows.

findings.title: Windows probe VM state (Track B, runtime)
findings.body:
- VM `unraidvm` (Unraid, Tailscale `100.88.38.86`) is reachable through `src/tools/vm.sh`. It runs Windows 10 19045 with 4 GB RAM, an Intel Arc B580 passed through (driver 32.0.101.9150), and `cdb` 10.0.26100.1. `C:\games\PES2021\PES2021.exe` SHA-256 is `58964C5A…45AD9`, the pinned exe.
- The pinned exe is the CPY release: `CPY.ini`, `steam_api64.dll` and `steamclient64.dll` sit next to it, on the Mac and on the VM.
- **The game does not start on the VM.** Launched normally in session 1 (scheduled task `/it`) and under `cdb` (`sxd -c2` on av): second-chance access violation at `0x141685425` `or dword [rbx+14h],1`, with `rbx` = the first argument = null. The caller `0x1419582CA` passes the result of looking up `"MainRender"` (`0x142A80F10`) through `0x1423C4700`, so the render object was never created. Stack: main thread, `0x1419582CF` <- `0x141957E8B` <- `0x140400695` <- `0x1403FF82A` <- `0x1402279AF`. **probable** cause: no display is attached to the Arc. `Win32_VideoController` shows no current resolution, `WmiMonitorBasicDisplayParams` lists no active monitor, and the QXL and remote adapters are not present. No `Documents\KONAMI\eFootball PES 2021` settings folder exists.
- Blocks P1 to P4. Needs a display on the Arc (monitor, HDMI/DP dummy plug, or a virtual display driver) and a way to see and drive the game remotely. 4 GB RAM is also below PES 2021's stated 8 GB.
- Later the same day: the VM now has 8 GB RAM. The VM was shut down gracefully, then `virsh setmaxmem`/`setmem 8G --config` on the Unraid host (`src/tools/vmhost.sh`), and Windows reports 8187 MB. The VM XML from before the change is saved on the host in `/boot/config/win10-before-8g.xml`. pesrecomp's screenshots from 2026-10-22 show PES at "Press Any Button" on this VM (windowed, 1280x800, under cdb). At that time the VM had a virtual QXL display, which the Arc passthrough later replaced. This supports the missing-display cause. The Sunshine MSI, the VDD driver and nefcon are downloaded to `C:\pesvm\dl`. Their install (`src/tools/vm_install_display.ps1`) was refused by the auto-mode permission check and is waiting on the user.

findings.title: VM can run the game; display and streaming (Track B, runtime)
findings.body:
- The startup crash at `0x141685425` is fixed by a display. The Virtual Display Driver (VDD 25.7.23, device `Root\MttVDD`, settings `C:\VirtualDisplayDriver\vdd_settings.xml`) gives Windows a monitor. PES then creates MainRender and reaches the title screen. This confirms the missing-display cause from the earlier entry. **confirmed** (crash before, title screen after, same exe).
- Sunshine (service `SunshineService`) streams the VM to Moonlight on the Mac. Install: `src/tools/vm_install_display.ps1`. Web UI login is in `private-reference/vm-sunshine.txt`. Lessons: the web UI needs `csrf_allowed_origins = https://100.88.38.86:47990` in `sunshine.conf`; two paired records with the same client cert make Sunshine reject that client ("certificate verification failed"), so keep one record per cert; Moonlight must store the server cert (`hosts.1.srvcert`) or it asks to pair every time.
- The game must start with working directory `C:\games\PES2021`. From `System32` (the scheduled-task default), `Fox/Scripts/Gr/init.lua` fails to load and the game stops with a DEADBEEF fatal at `0x14195849C`. Launchers `cd /d` first and run in session 1 through `schtasks /it`.
- VM disk: 1.9 GB free on `C:`. Keep cdb logs small.

findings.title: P1 result, foul thresholds at run time (Track B, verified against the game)
findings.body:
Setup: `tests/behaviour/cdb/p1_thresholds.txt`, three `ba e1` hardware breakpoints (no code bytes changed): entry `0x143FA8760` (caller, out pointer, word at `0x1482B3DC8`), `0x143FA87F8` (ClassifyFoulZone result in `eax`, floats at `[rsp+0x20]`, `[rsp+0x28]`), `0x143FA881B` (the three output bytes). One full CPU-vs-CPU match in Master League with the user as coach (the only CPU-vs-CPU route the user found; not an exhibition). 6 calls. Thresholds may depend on competition or referee settings, so this result holds for an ML league match only. These are calls, not counted fouls: whether every call is a foul given (or also a judged challenge with no foul) is **not checked**; compare with the match's foul count and capture the ScoreToSeverity output next time. Raw lines are in `tests/behaviour/referee/p1_thresholds_2026-11-03.tsv`.

- Runtime word at `0x1482B3DC8` = `0x00C0` on all 6 hits, the same as the file value. `0x00C0 ^ 0x50FC` = `0x503C`, so 60, 80. **confirmed**.
- T3 = 110 on 6/6. **confirmed** for this match.
- Bit 11 of the ClassifyFoulZone result was set on 2 hits; both gave 60/80. It was clear on 4 hits; all gave 40/80. Bit 10 (`0x400`) never appeared. **confirmed** that bit 11 selects the pair (6/6 calls, both cases seen at least twice).
- Every call came from `0x143F716AF`, inside the ScoreToSeverity body. In this match GetFoulThresholds had no other caller.
- Position: the 60/80 hits had x = 38.09 and -36.76, |y| <= 11.45. The 40/80 hits had |x| <= 28.10. On a 105 x 68 m pitch with the centre at 0 (**guess**: units and origin not checked), the 60/80 calls sit inside the two penalty areas (|x| > 36, |y| < 20.16). Bit 11 came up at both ends. Which box it means (own or attacked, relative to the fouling team) is still **not settled**: the team identity and attack direction were not captured.
- Port: `foul_thresholds` in `src/game/referee/foul_severity.cpp` reproduces all 6 captured outputs. `ctest -R foul_severity` now replays the TSV. Mutation: changing the first 60/80 row's eax to `0xa1` fails the test. Port status stays `reimplemented` until P1's acceptance (3 matches) is met.
- Still open: 2 more matches for P1's acceptance; capture the fouling team and its attack direction to settle the box meaning; severity outputs (ScoreToSeverity exit) were not captured.

findings.title: P2 to P4 result, Master League creation (Track B, runtime)
findings.body:
Setup: `tests/behaviour/cdb/p234/`, three `ba e1` entry breakpoints, one run. The user created a new Master League (coach mode) and simulated to the first fixture. Probe lines are in `tests/behaviour/competition/p234_2026-11-03.txt`.

- **P3, BuildSeason `0x1413156E0`:** called once, at creation, from `0x1413155DF` inside EventDriver `0x141314FC0`, on a worker thread. **confirmed** (one run). The third argument is a vector `{begin, end, capacity}`, but its elements are **u16, not 20-byte entries**: 91 values (182 bytes). Values look like `id | slot << 10`: `0x0002, 0x0402 … 0x2002` is id 2 with slots 0 to 8. **guess** for that split. 63 distinct low-10-bit ids: 1–7, 17–28, 30, 50, 53, 59, 79–92, 95, 115–118, 122–125, 128–130, 133–137, 141, 142, 147, 148, 151, 155, 156, 159, 172, 175.
- FL's sample ids (67 68 76 93 94 96 97 98 119 162) are **none** of these 63. FL's "55 ids, static in the exe" does not match this build's runtime list. The full list, its first 8 values, and a 6-value tail are not in the exe file as u16, u32 or u8 runs. This supports the earlier **guess** that the list is built at run time. Still open: what builds it.
- **P4, EventDriver `0x141314FC0`:** 30 calls (cap reached), all with return address `0x141300B47`, on 12 different `rcx` objects. The call at `0x141300B42` targets `0x141315DF0`, not EventDriver. So `0x141315DF0` reaches EventDriver without pushing a return address (tail jump, **probable**, not read). Objects look like list nodes: `[rcx]` points 0x10 below another node's `rcx`. The first object was the one passed to BuildSeason. The name stays **guess**: this is a per-node handler, and only one call led to BuildSeason.
- **P2, GetOrBlank `0x1414BB000`:** all 400 captured calls happened at boot, before creation. They came from `0x1414CB73D` (305) and `0x1414F80AB` (95), with one EditData base, `mode` (edit+0x183789C) = 0 and `count` (edit+0xD0BCF4) = 214. At BuildSeason the same base read `count` = 199 and `mode` = 2 (the linear lookup capped at 300). So both are runtime state, and creation switches the table to linear lookup. **confirmed** (one run). The first 40 records at creation have ascending u16 ids `0x0001–0x002E` with gaps, `+0x80` non-decreasing (1 to 0x24), and `+0x84` in {1, 2, 3}. Sorted ascending holds for those 40 (**probable** for the whole table).
- Not settled: the regulation id layout (record ids seen are all below 0x400, so the slot bits never appear); what `+0x80` and `+0x84` mean.

findings.title: where the season include list comes from (Track B, static plus runtime)
findings.body:
Static read of EventDriver `0x141314FC0` and its helpers (Ghidra), checked against the P3 capture.

- `0x14157E850` loads 15 event entries of 20 bytes from `0x14298CA30`: `{key, league, year, league2, year2}`. For event 13 it bumps two fields when the date year is 2020 or 2021. EventDriver keeps events whose `league` equals the u16 at `edit+0x1642A1C`, and whose `year` is -1, matches the date year, or `0x14149F4F0` returns 7. It builds a second list from `league2`/`year2`. Events 0 and 3 have league 181 (0xB5). 0xB5 appears in the captured BuildSeason stack, and BuildSeason's second argument held 2 values. So this ML ran with league 181 and events {0, 3}. **probable** (the u16 at `edit+0x1642A1C` was not read directly).
- `0x14157E760` copies a static table at `0x14298CB60`: 246 entries of 20 bytes. Each entry has a u16 regulation id at +0 and a u32 event key at +16. EventDriver drops entries whose id is not in EditData's regulation table, then keeps entries whose key is a selected event. `0x140CC7F20` pushes the entry's first u16 into the include list (BuildSeason's third argument).
- Check: the 91 captured include ids appear **in order** in the static table, and all selected entries have key 0 or 3. **confirmed** (static table plus one runtime capture). This corrects the earlier entries: the list **is** static data in the exe, stored at a 20-byte stride, which is why the contiguous u16 search found nothing. It is filtered at run time. FL's "static in the exe" holds in that sense; their sample ids still do not appear as regulation ids (different numbering, not checked).
- Not checked: why some key-0 entries were left out (presumably their ids are missing from EditData); what `0x14149F4F0`'s value 7 means; and the other path, `0x141315FD0` / `0x141314350` with the league2 list.
- P1 aside: Aoba's wiki (PDF the user supplied, 2026-11-03) names `0x140A72E70` "PenaltyAreaCheck", with 0x800 = inside the box, marked "implied". The two 0x800 calls in P1 sat deep at each end, which fits. Own or attacked box is still open.

findings.title: correction from FootballLife's repo (Track B)
findings.body:
FL's repo (`FootballLife-new-leagues-main`, MIT) explains two things in the include-list entry above.
- `edit+0x1642A1C` is the **current-day counter** (u16), not a league id (FL `research-findings.md` ~3546, 4164; `league-phase-swiss-decode.md` 282). So field 1 of the event table at `0x14298CA30` is a **day**. Events 0 and 3 fire on day 181 (0xB5, season start), and EventDriver fires the season events due today. The earlier "league 181" reading is wrong. **probable** (FL plus the matching 0xB5 on the captured stack). This supports the name EventDriver; it stays `probable`.
- High bits of a regulation id are a **replica index**: `replica_rid = master + (group+1) * 1024` (FL ~11232; "replicas 1026 + 1024k" in `league-phase-swiss-decode.md`). In the capture, `0x0402 … 0x2002` are group replicas 1 to 8 of regulation 2. This replaces the earlier `slot << 10` **guess**. **probable**.
- FL calls regulation 17 (0x11) the Premier League; 0x11 is in the captured list. A full id-to-name map is not in FL's docs; it should come from the game's competition database.

findings.title: the include list, named (Track B/C, static data)
findings.body:
Read `common/etc/pesdb/CompetitionRegulation.bin` through our VFS and WESYS unwrap: 212 rows of 2352 bytes. Layout from FL (`research-findings.md` ~136, ~220): u16 regulation id at +2, competition id at +8, English name at +0x1E0, internal code at +0x41F (offsets read on row 0, used for all rows). **probable** (FL layout, every row decoded to a sensible code).

- 61 of the 63 included ids are rows in the file. Grouped: UEFA (2–7: UCL playoff, groups, knockout; UEL groups, knockout; Super Cup). League, cup and super cup for England, Italy, Spain, France, Netherlands, Portugal and Argentina (17–28, 30, 59, 86–92). Second divisions and play-offs for England, Spain, France and Italy (79–85). Belgium, Russia, Switzerland, Turkey, Scotland and Denmark with their split phases (115–159). The PES fantasy competitions (50, 53, 95). In short, the Master League world.
- 172 and 175 are not in the file. At boot the game's table held 214 rows, 2 more than the file, so those two are probably added at run time. **guess**.
- FL's sample ids (67 68 76 93 94 96 97 98 119 162) look like **competition ids** (+8), not regulation ids. 67 is Spain D2, 68 France D2, 76 Supercoppa Italiana, 119 Turkey D1. The other six are not competition ids in this file, so they may be FL's own additions. **guess**.
- Next (Track C): add a `CompetitionRegulation` reader to `src/engine/formats/pesdb/` (golden count 212), then port the include-list selection into `src/game/` with a replay test against `tests/behaviour/competition/p234_2026-11-03.txt`.

findings.title: CompetitionRegulation reader and season selection port (Track C)
findings.body:
- `src/engine/formats/pesdb/`: `parse_regulations` reads `CompetitionRegulation.bin` (2352-byte records): id, parent, competition id, group, team count, seeded flag, English name, code. Golden: 212 rows, dump hash pinned in `tests/golden/pesdb/tables.txt` (6/6 tables match with `PES_DATA`). Agrees with FL's documented rows: UCL group stage 32 teams seeded, World Cup 34 groups / 35 knockout, replica 1026 points at parent 2. Codes are cut at 31 characters in the file itself (`UEFA_CHAMPIONS_LEAGUE_GROUPSTAG`); the next language string starts right after. **probable** (FL layout plus these checks).
- `src/game/competition/season_select.{h,cpp}`: `select_season` ports EventDriver's selection step (events due today; include table filtered by the regulations that exist), fidelity behavioural. `tests/game/season_select_test.cpp`: unit cases (year gate > 2019, low-2-bit year match, any-year mode, existence filter, order), plus a replay with `PES_DATA` that reads both tables from the exe and checks against the P3 capture. Result: events {0, 3} fire on day 181. With the file's ids plus the captured ids as "existing", the captured 91 ids are the selection, in order, minus exactly 5 ids. Mutation: `ev_day <= day` gives 3 failures.
- The 5 left out are in the file but were absent from the save at creation: 99 KONAMI League, 149/150 Denmark bottom round groups A/B, 157/158 Belgium play-off groups A/B. 172 and 175 were present live but are not in the file. So the save's regulation table at creation is not the file (214 rows at boot, 199 at creation). **confirmed** that the sets differ; why is open. `p3hit.txt` now dumps every live record id at BuildSeason, so the next ML capture can feed the replay the real table.
- Port tracking: `db/seeds/ports/competition.tsv` marks EventDriver `reimplemented`, `behavioural`.

findings.title: second Master League capture: live regulation table and P1 with team and direction (Track B/C, runtime)
findings.body:
Setup: `tests/behaviour/cdb/p234/` (P2–P4 until BuildSeason, which dumps the whole live regulation table and then re-arms the breakpoints as P1). One run, cdb log kept in `private-reference/vm-probe2/out/run_2026-11-03b.log`. The user created another new Master League (coach), simulated to the first fixture, played one CPU-vs-CPU match, then half of a second. The game froze when the user opened the replay editor at half time. The log ends cleanly after a P1 hit, with no AV line, and cdb was still attached and running. So the freeze is probably not a probe stop. **guess** (the hung process was not inspected).

**Season selection (probes P2/P3).** Data: `tests/behaviour/competition/p234_2026-11-03b.txt`.
- The include list is identical to the first capture (91 ids, same order). **confirmed** (two runs).
- The live table at BuildSeason has 199 rows, the same count as the first run. Ids 99, 149, 150, 157 and 158 are not among them. That accounts for all 5 ids the first replay left out.
- `season_select_test` now filters on the live table. The selection then **equals** the captured list exactly, in order. Fidelity is raised to `exact` (`db/seeds/ports/competition.tsv`). **confirmed** for this input (day 181, one save state).
- Still open: why the save's table differs from the file. The file has 212 rows; the live table has 199.

**Fouls (probe P1).** Data: `tests/behaviour/referee/p1_thresholds_2026-11-03b.tsv`, 9 calls. All come from `0x143f716af`, with word 0x00c0. None has bit 11 set, and every one gets thresholds 40/80/110. These rows replay in `foul_severity_test` (ctest `foul_severity_ml2`).
- **Direction:** in all 9 calls, the sign of the direction byte (`[team+0x254]`, 1 or 255 = -1) equals the sign of the foul's x. **confirmed** (9/9, 8 distinct incidents).
- **Halves:** the direction flips between calls 3 and 4, and flips back between calls 6 and 7. Before the first flip, team 0 (players 0–10) is +1 and team 1 is -1. Between the flips it is the other way round. After the second flip, team 1 is -1 again. That fits sides changing at half time. So calls 1–6 would be match 1 and calls 7–9 the first half of match 2. **probable**.
- **Calls are not fouls:** calls 7 and 8 have the same player and the same x/y, but scores 17 and 58. So one incident was scored twice, and the score has a random or state-dependent part. Calls 7 and 8 are the same incident. **confirmed**. Why scored twice is **guess**. The match-1 split from the previous point gives 6 calls, 3 per team. The user read fouls 2 and 3 from the match stats, so at least one call was not counted as a foul. **probable** (depends on the split).
- What `[team+0x254]` means is still open. It could be the attacking direction or the side of the team's own goal. That decides whether the earlier bit-11 calls (|x| ≈ 37) were in the fouling team's own box or the attacked box.

findings.title: team direction and the 60/80 box, settled statically (Track B)
findings.body:
Static read (Ghidra, `private-reference/pc/decomp/teamdir/`) of every byte write to `+0x254`. A byte-pattern search over the executable sections found 11 writes; one is a one-line setter.

- `TeamData+0x254` is written once per update by `Match_Team_SetDirection` `0x140A42570`. Its only caller is `0x1404FE9C0`, at `0x1404FEBAB`. The value comes from `Match_Team_ComputeDirection` `0x1404F4AE0`, which returns +1 or -1 per team. The sign depends on the match period at `state+0x1168` (cases 0–9) and a flag at `state+0x1574`. So the value flips between periods. This matches the half-time flips seen in the second P1 capture. **probable**.
- `Referee_Judge_PackageFoulEvent` `0x1405B8000` classifies the foul spot with the same team's direction:
  - bit 11 clear: restart type 5 at the foul spot;
  - bit 11 set: restart type 6, at the position from `Match_Restart_GetPosition` `0x14050D280`.
  For type 6 that function returns `(sign(foul_x) * geom[8], 0)`: a fixed point on the pitch's centre line at the foul's end. That is the penalty spot. So bit 11 means "penalty". **probable** (geom[8] not read at run time; the box edge p[6] fits |x| ≈ 36, and the first capture's two bit-11 calls were at |x| 36.8 and 38.1).
- Answer to the open question: a penalty is awarded in the box the fouling team defends. So **the 60/80 thresholds apply to fouls inside the fouling team's own penalty area**, not the box it attacks. **probable**. This does not depend on which of DecideFoul's two players is the fouler.
  - Register pass-through: ScoreToSeverity hands DecideFoul's `param_2` to GetFoulThresholds, and P1's `player` (esi) is that `param_2`. P1's r9 player was always on the other team.
  - If `param_2` is the fouler, `+0x254` points to the team's own goal. If it is the fouled player, `+0x254` is the attacking direction. **guess** for the first reading: `param_3` matches `FUN_140A62690`'s per-team player, which fits a ball holder, but that is not read.
- Either reading gives the same picture: all 9 P1 calls in the second capture were in the half the fouling team defends.
- Side note, not checked further: DecideFoul treats bit 11 specially when picking the card. At its line 336, with 0x800 set, severities 3–4 can be lowered to 1, or 4 to 3, depending on `0x1405B7390` (**guess**: a rule such as softer punishment for a penalty foul).

findings.title: skeptic review of today's names and claims (Track B/C)
findings.body:
pes-skeptic did static reads only, plus the replay test. It ran no new decompiles. Results and the fixes made:

- **Season tables and loaders hold.** The event table is 15 × 20 bytes and the include table 246 × 20 bytes; the loop counts are 0xf and 0xf6. Two wording fixes:
  - `0x14157E760` has one direct caller, plus a DATA ref at `0x143BD2F70`.
  - `0x14157E850` has 4 more direct callers.
- **Naming collision fixed:** the guess row `0x1434EECC0` also carried the name `Competition_SeasonEventTable`. It is renamed `Competition_RegulationSlotTable_Unknown`.
- **FootballLife readings hold (probable).** The event table's day field holds values like 332 and 360, which cannot be regulation or league ids. All 107 include ids ≥ 1024 have a high part (id >> 10) of 1–12, and their low 10 bits are master ids in the same table.
- **"exact" was overclaimed; fixed.**
  - The loader `0x14157E850` adds 1 to year and year2 of key-13 rows when the date year is 2020 or 2021. It does this only if the packed date differs from the runtime global `0x1437F47F8`. I read this in the decompile myself.
  - Without the bump, key 13 (day 216, stored year 2019) never fires in 2020, so 8 include entries would be lost.
  - Now ported as `apply_loader_year_bump`. Tests: a unit case, and a replay check that the real key-13 row fires on day 216 of 2020. A mutation that removes the bump fails the unit case.
  - Fidelity is back to `behavioural`. Gaps: the any-year mode (`0x14149F4F0 == 7`) is not exercised, the null-state early return is not ported, and the global's condition is not read.
- **Penalty inference holds, more strongly than stated.** The constants in `Match_Restart_GetPosition` give the restart types:

  | Type | Restart |
  |---|---|
  | 1, 7 | (0, 0), kickoff |
  | 2 | throw-in |
  | 3 | goal kick |
  | 4 | corner |
  | 5 | foul spot (free kick) |
  | 6 | (±geom[8], 0), the penalty spot |

  `PackageFoulEvent` sends only 0x800 to type 6; 0x400 (the other box) gets a free kick. So exactly one box gives penalties: the one the fouling team defends. That does not depend on which player is the fouler. geom[8] is built at run time and not found in static data, so it stays **probable**.
- **Correction to the previous entry.** "All 9 P1 calls were in the half the fouling team defends" holds only if P1's `player` is the fouler and `+0x254` points to the team's own goal. The 9/9 sign match cannot tell this pairing from the opposite one. Which player is the fouler, and what `+0x254` means, stay open.
- **Direction byte, weakened wording.**
  - `Match_Team_ComputeDirection` returns ±1 only for periods 0–9; its default case returns a low byte of 0.
  - `+0x254` is also written at construction (`0x141A33D96` = 1), copied (`0x1404167B3`, `0x1415D9831`) and loaded from a stream (`0x14215D35E`, likely replay).
  - The static link is missing: the setter's object (`*(state+0x6D50)`) is not shown to be the `Match_World_GetTeamData` object the referee reads. Only the run-time flip pattern supports that.

findings.title: why the live regulation table has 199 rows, not 212 (Track A/B)
findings.body:
- **Boot 214 = the update pack, confirmed.** `download/dt80_100E_x64.cpk` (the game's update data pack) has its own `common/etc/pesdb/CompetitionRegulation.bin` with **214 rows**: the boot count. It holds 172 (`BELGIUM_D1_LEAGUE_4`, Play-Offs Group B, 4 teams) and 175 (`DENMARK_D1_LEAGUE_4`, Play-Offs Group B, 6 teams), the two ids missing from `Data/`. The update restructures both leagues' play-offs:
  - Belgium: 156 + 172 replace 157/158.
  - Denmark: 148 + 175 replace 149/150, and 147 drops from 14 to 12 teams.

  `Data/` holds the file only in dt00 and dt10 (212 rows; our VFS serves dt10). Our VFS mounts only `Data/`, so every golden and replay that reads pesdb tables reads the pre-update data. **confirmed** (file read, counts, ids; parsed with our reader into `private-reference/pesdb-dump/CompetitionRegulation_dt80.txt`).
- **At Master League creation, 15 rows go: 214 → 199, confirmed.** The 15:
  - the placeholder KONAMI Cup: 47, 48 and 8 group replicas, comp 37 `FAKE_KONAMI`;
  - KONAMI League: 99, comp 86;
  - the obsolete Denmark and Belgium groups: 149, 150, 157, 158.

  Every other row of the update file is live, and nothing else is.
- **Ruled out as the selector:**
  - a field in the record: a byte- and bit-level scan of all 2352 bytes finds nothing that splits the 15 from the 199 except the id;
  - a delete list: the pesdb folder has `CoachDeleteList` and `PlayerDeleteList`, but no regulation delete list;
  - the season include table: all 15 are in it.
- **Mechanism, partly read.** Only two instructions write the count at `edit+0xD0BCF4`:
  - `Competition_RegulationLoader_BuildTable` (`0x1414F1D38`), at boot;
  - `Edit_Tables_RecountSlots` `0x1414BC0A0`, which counts the 300 slots whose u16 id is not 0xFFFF.

  Among its 10 callers, `Competition_RegulationTable_RebuildFromList` `0x14126F7E0` (**guess**) copies the 0x314-byte records of a vector at `obj+0x48..0x50` (obj = `DAT_1436FED48`) into the slots, then recounts. So the live table at creation is probably that vector's contents, and the 15 were never in it. **probable**. Who fills the vector, and by what rule, is open. It might come from the save or the option file, or from a filter by competition.
- **Next check (runtime, one VM session):** at boot, after the first P2 hit, put a `ba w2` on the id of slot 149 (its rank in the sorted 214-row table) and print `kb` when it changes. Alternatively, break on `0x14126F7E0` and dump the vector's ids and its fill site.
- **Engine follow-up (Track C):** the VFS should mount `download/` above `Data/`, as the game does (DpFileList, not read yet). Then the pesdb goldens should be re-pinned on the post-update tables.

findings.title: VFS mounts the update pack; pesdb goldens re-pinned on post-update data (Track A/C)
findings.body:
- `Vfs::mount_game(data_dir)` mounts `Data/`, then `data_dir/../download` on top, so the update pack wins. `download/DpFileList.bin` lists only `dt80_100E_x64.cpk`; the list is not parsed yet, which is a marked shortcut. Used by `pes_host --data`, `pesdb_golden_test` and `season_select_test`. Unit test: synthetic `Data/` + `download/` CPKs; the download copy wins, and a missing download folder is fine.
- All six pesdb tables now come from `dt80_100E_x64.cpk`. Four differ from the pre-update data: Player 17782 → 18452, Team 663 → 669, CompetitionEntry 1291 → 1283, CompetitionRegulation 212 → 214. Competition (91) and CompetitionKind (9) are unchanged.
  - The FootballLife-based Python oracle, run on the same extracted bins, gives dumps byte-identical to ours for the five tables it covers. **confirmed**.
  - CompetitionRegulation has no oracle; its hash is our own dump. The diff from the old data is only real format updates: 172 and 175 added; Denmark 141/147 14 → 12 teams, 148 renamed, 151 5 → 2; Belgium 156 6 → 4, 159 3 → 2; Russia 116 18 → 16.
- `season_select_test` now also pins the boot-to-creation step: the live table equals the 214-row update file minus exactly the 15 ids (47, 48, 99, 149, 150, 157, 158 and the 8 KONAMI Cup replicas), with nothing live that the file lacks. **confirmed** (one capture's live table; the rule that picks the 15 is still open, see the previous entry).

findings.title: the Master League regulation filter, found and ported (Track B/C, runtime + static)
findings.body:
Two VM runs with `tests/behaviour/cdb/regdrop/`, each a new Master League simulated to the first fixture. Data: `tests/behaviour/competition/regdrop_2026-11-03.txt`.

**Sequence at creation (confirmed, two runs):**
1. The regulation count goes to 0, then back to 214: the table is reloaded from the update file through the boot loader path (`0x1414F6CB3`).
2. The global `0x1436FED48` gets a new source object.
3. A loop walks every slot of the reloaded table and pushes kept records onto `obj+0x48` with `Vector_Regulation_PushBack` `0x140F3AE90`. The VW probe saw 199 pushes, one id each, in table order. The push returns to `0x141264C22`; the caller is `0x1412670F3`.
4. `Competition_RegulationTable_RebuildFromList` copies the 199 into the table, and the count becomes 199.

**The loop's two filters (static read of `0x141264C22`'s loop, `0x1412645B0`, `0x141547070`):**
- `Competition_ML_IsExcludedRegulationId` `0x141547070` returns true for ids 149–150 and 157–158 (`0x95`/`0x96`, `0x9D`/`0x9E`). So the old Denmark and Belgium groups are **hard-coded**. **confirmed**.
- `Competition_ML_SkipRegulation` `0x1412645B0` keeps a record only if all of these hold:
  - `+0x30C` bits 7–12 are non-zero and not 0x1D;
  - `+0x308` bits 23–28 are in 1–0x30 or above 0x35;
  - the id is not 0xB1 (177).

  It also has a skip path on the flag `edit+0x1789466` and `+0x30C` bit 21, via three helper checks; that path is not read.
- In the file, the `+0x308` field is the 6 bits at bit 108 (byte 0xD, bit 4). Values: 1–48 on all 199 kept rows, and 49, 50 or 52 on all 11 KONAMI rows. Its meaning is unknown, so it is called `ml_class`. The mapping from memory field to file bits is **probable**: the values match exactly, but the parser is not read.
- The other runtime-only conditions are not needed to reproduce the shipped data.

**Port:** `ml_keeps_regulation(id, ml_class)` in `src/game/competition/season_select.cpp`, plus `CompetitionRegulation::ml_class` in the pesdb reader. Applied to the update file, it gives **exactly** the 199 live ids. `season_select_test` checks this against the capture, with unit cases on both sides of each condition. Fidelity: `behavioural`, because the two runtime-only conditions and the bit-21 path are not ported. That closes the 199-vs-212 question:
- 212 is the pre-update file;
- 214 is the update file;
- 199 is what this filter keeps.

findings.title: league fixtures, round table read and ported (Track B/C, static)
cross-reference with Aoba's wiki (Track B)
findings.body:
Full text of the PDF the user supplied is in `private-reference/aoba/aoba.txt` (102 pages, pypdf). It names 133 functions, but pesrecomp's import only brought in 68 of them. It does not cover competitions, seasons or fixtures; those are cross-checked against FootballLife instead. On the referee code it agrees with our independently derived names on all 18 functions both cover.

Against today's findings:
- **`TeamData+0x254`**: Aoba calls it **AttackDirection** (+1/-1, "which goal is forward"; PES 2017 at +252). That resolves the open pairing from the skeptic entry:
  - ClassifyFoulZone sets 0x800 when `dir * x > 0`, and that bit is the penalty box (restart type 6).
  - With dir as the attacking direction, the team whose direction is used must be the **fouled** team.
  - So `Referee_Judge_DecideFoul`'s `param_2` (and P1's `player`/esi) is the fouled player, and `param_3` (P1's r9) the fouler.

  **probable** (Aoba plus a consistent static picture). Not runtime-checked: a check would compare `player` against the match's foul list. The 9/9 sign match then says each foul was in the half the fouled team attacks, which is the fouler's own half. The conclusion "60/80 applies in the fouling team's own box" is unchanged. Struct row renamed `attack_direction`.
- **Free kick vs penalty**: Aoba says `CardEventPackager` (`0x1405B8000`) "determines FK/PEN". That independently supports restart type 5 = free kick and 6 = penalty.
- **Card softening inside the box**: the helper is `0x1405B7390`, which Aoba (and our seeds) call IsDOGSO. With 0x800 set, DecideFoul lowers severity 3–4 to 1, or 4 to 3, depending on DOGSO. That is the real-world rule that a penalty foul denying a goal chance gets a lesser card. **probable** (Aoba plus the read).
- **Disagreement**: Aoba describes the pitch geometry at `gMatchContext+0x2AA8` as an 8-float structure. ClassifyFoulZone reads p[0..7] and p[0x11], and Match_Restart_GetPosition reads p[8] (the penalty spot). So the structure is at least 0x12 floats.
- Not yet done: import the ~65 PDF names pesrecomp missed, as Aoba seeds marked probable. Most are player AI (playing styles, runs, marking), outside current work. The parse needs care, because the PDF mixes in PES 2020 addresses.

findings.title: league round table confirmed at run time (Track B/C)
PES 2020 exe available as a read-only cross-reference (Track B)
findings.body:
The user supplied the PES 2020 they own as `PES2020 voices38/` (git-ignored). `PES2020.exe` details:
- SHA-256 `79f95f53f5d2717aef5fa3f8cd730e18cc5e5e4272f4da7b778c83fa76a7c69d`;
- 396 MB, PE timestamp 1594063932 (2020-07-06), image base 140000000 (same as 2021);
- 16 sections: `.xdata` holds the main code (0x24DBE00 raw) and `.idata` is 0x15334260 bytes.

The code is readable with capstone. PES 2020 addresses are written here as `sub_…`, so the naming check does not take them for 2021 addresses. Use: read-only, to check our 2021 readings; carry-over per function follows guide section 8.

First check, of Aoba's "plaintext constants" claim for the referee:
- PES 2020's GetFoulThresholds `sub_146004100` loads `byte [team+0x254]` into the zone call `sub_140A73270` (ClassifyFoulZone) and writes T3 = `0x6E` unconditionally.
- On `bt eax, 0xB` it writes `word 0x503C` (60/80) when the bit is set, else `0x5028` (40/80). These are plaintext immediates where 2021 uses `word[0x1482B3DC8] ^ 0x50FC`.

That agrees with the 2021 run-time value (word 0x00C0, so 60) and with our port. **confirmed** (two builds plus run time).

Nearby PES 2020 counterparts seen in passing, all **probable**: GetTeamData is `sub_140A489F0` (2021 `0x140A48A30`) and GetFoulPosition is `sub_1405B88B0`. `sub_1405BA040` matches the start of 2021's CardEventPackager (same `r9d` team split, `[ctx+0x270]` read).

findings.title: all league tables and the big-league calendar confirmed at run time (Track B/C)
findings.body:
Probe v2 (`tests/behaviour/cdb/fixtures/`), one new Master League simulated to the first fixture. Data: `tests/behaviour/competition/fixtures_2026-11-03.txt`, which replaces the regulation-17-only capture.

The probe dumped every RoundTable result at its shared return `0x1413F38C0`, plus the first date list per regulation id from `Competition_Calendar_GetRoundDates` `0x14157F810`. That lookup runs once per match entry, so breaking on it makes creation very slow, but the game did not hang.

- **Round tables:** all 20 leagues match `league_round_table`, **12,416 cells, 0 differences**. They cover 4–24 teams and 1, 2, 3 and 4 legs: Switzerland 117 has 10 teams × 4 legs, and Scotland 134 has 12 × 3. **confirmed**. No league in the shipped data has an odd team count, so the bye path is checked only by the property tests.
- **Big-league calendar** (date case 5; FootballLife lists ids 17–22, 50, 99, 116, 118). The helper `Competition_Calendar_BigLeague` `0x141582550`:
  - copies 38 entries `{day, round, flags = 2}` from `0x14298ED80`, days 233 (21 Aug) through 142 (22 May);
  - when the id exists (`0x14151D190`), drops the rounds listed for the league size via `Competition_Calendar_DropRounds` `0x14157E650`: under 15 teams the 12 at `0x14298EF78`, under 17 the 8 at `0x14298EF58`, under 19 the 4 at `0x14298EF48`;
  - erases the first entry per listed round, then renumbers.

  The size field is regulation `+0x308` bits 16–22, the same team count the setup reads. The resulting lengths, 38/34/30/26, are exactly 2(n − 1) for 20/18/16/14 teams.
- **Port:** `big_league_calendar`, which reads the four tables from the exe at test time. All **9** case-5 date lists in the capture match it entry by entry: 17–20 and 50 (20 teams), 21, 22 and 118 (18), and 116 (16). **confirmed**. Moving the 17-team threshold fails 24 checks. The 14-team branch is not exercised by the shipped data.
- **Other date cases** are captured but not ported: 58 lists in all. Examples: 79 (Championship) has 46 entries, 80 has 42, Switzerland 117 has 36 starting on day 226, 30 has 23, and cups such as 23–28 have 5–12. Ids 115, 133 and 141 return none.
- Next: how fixture records take a day from these lists (`0x141350B40` / `0x141350290`; FootballLife describes the match lookup by competition key), and the remaining date cases.

findings.title: PES 2015 supplied; RTTI class names in 2021 (Track B)
findings.body:
- The user supplied PES 2015 (owned), as `Pro Evolution Soccer 2015/` (git-ignored). `PES2015.exe`: SHA-256 `71ed2c56fce2adb69d9b7b650a14432e0ae803ca53944ef5d6feb2e8b27ab4d5`, **32-bit x86** (PE32, base 400000), PE timestamp 2014-10-29, 37 MB. Being 32-bit, its code cannot match 2021 by bytes. Its use is class names and structure, per guide section 8 step 3.
- RTTI type names (`.?AV…@@` / `.?AU…@@`): 7,227 in 2015 and **11,435 in our 2021 exe**; 4,371 are shared, 2,856 appear only in 2015 and 7,064 only in 2021.
  - The 2015-only names are mostly global, menu, process, `rs` and `commandautomake`, plus 37 under `ai`.
  - The 2021 names include match and season classes, e.g. `OwnerSeasonTaskJudge` tasks, league chapters, `AddFoul` and `AssistantRefereePropUnit`.

  So 2021 carries its own class names. Mapping its RTTI (type descriptor → complete object locator → vtable) names classes and their virtual functions directly, without carrying anything over from 2015. **confirmed** (string counts); the vtable map is not built yet.
- `pt-pc-main/` (user-supplied, MIT, git-ignored) is a third-party native port of P.T., a Fox Engine title. It can serve as a read-only reference for Fox Engine formats later.

findings.title: fixture date cases ported, all 58 captured lists replay (Track C; pes-porter)
findings.body:
pes-porter ported the date lookup `Competition_Calendar_GetRoundDates` for every case seen in the capture: `fixture_dates(case, id, DateRegulation, DateCaseData)` in `src/game/competition/fixtures.{h,cpp}`. The case-5 logic became the generic `trim_calendar`. The test reads the id-to-case byte table and every list from the exe (table addresses are in `tests/game/fixtures_test.cpp`). **All 58 DT lists of the capture replay exactly**: 23 cases, day, round, flags and count. ctest `fixtures`. I re-ran it, and no game addresses remain under `src/`.

Case behaviours (pes-porter read the decompile and helper disassembly; **confirmed** by replay unless noted):
- **Verbatim list:** cases 2, 25, 34, 37.
- **Per-id lists for ids 2–6:** `Competition_Calendar_EuropeanCup` `0x141581410`. Ids 3 and 5 share a list, and id 5 gets day+1 from an `(id − 5)` rule.
- **List plus mode filter** (mode = in-memory `+0x300 >> 29`):
  - cases 6, 29, 31, 32, 38, 39, 43, 47 push the list first; cases 27 and 57 look up the regulation first.
  - Mode 0 (`0x14157F720`) erases flag-0 rows and turns flag 1 into 2. Mode 1 (`0x14157F790`) does the same only for rounds 53–54. Other modes change nothing.
- **By period** (`Competition_Regulation_GetPeriod` `0x141543910` = `+0x308 >> 23 & 0x3F`): cases 42, 51, 54. 12 selects the main list, 13–15 a second list.

  This is the same field as `ml_class` in the Master League filter (file bit 108). There, 1–48 was kept and 49–53 dropped, so it is probably a calendar or season-type code. That is a **guess**.
- **Trim by team count:** cases 5, 8, 22, 28. The first tier whose limit exceeds the team count supplies rounds to erase, then the rest are renumbered. Case 28 is the English 79–82: 46 entries, minus 8 below 21 teams or 4 below 23.
- **Case 62:** empty.

Unverified:
- **Mode** is not mapped to the file. The test supplies it per id, and modes 0 and 1 give the same list for several ids.
- **Id 120's team count** (16) is inferred.
- **Not exercised:** the period 13–15 lists and the not-found paths (unit-tested against the read only).
- **Not ported:** ids above 175 and any case not seen in the capture. These return `nullopt`.

Mutations moving a tier, the case-1 rule, the mode-1 rounds or the period value each fail the replay.

findings.title: league matches and their days, read and ported (Track B/C, static)
findings.body:
- **`Competition_FixtureBuilder_EmitLeague` `0x1413F4430`.** For each round r below the setup's total, then each leg, row i and column j > i, with both indices real teams (byes skipped): if `table[leg][i][j].round == r`, it allocates a match record (`0x1414BC710`). It sets `+4` to the regulation id plus `(r | 0x2000) << 16`, so round r sits in bits 16–27 and kind 2 in bits 28–29. Team i goes to `+0x18` when the cell's home flag is 1, else to `+0x14`; team j takes the other slot. The match is then appended to its round's fixture record (`0x141579EE0` lookup, or `0x141579DB0` to allocate), at most 16 entries. Overflow, or a full match table, drops the match silently, as FootballLife reported. **probable** (read).
- **`Competition_Season_ScheduleMatches` `0x141350B40`** walks each round's fixture record, up to 16 entries of up to 3 match ids. For each match it takes the **first** date entry whose round equals record bits 16–27 and whose flags equal bits 28–29, then calls `Competition_Calendar_FileMatchOnDay` `0x141350290`. That function stores the match index in the day record at `edit+0x16038A8 + day × 0x2C4`: 280 u16 slots, with the count in slot 0x118. It also handles a 0x36-over-0x35 replacement rule, then sets date and kickoff fields. **probable** (read; agrees with FootballLife).
- **Port:** `league_matches(table, teams)` (creation order, slots `+0x14`/`+0x18`) and `match_day(dates, round, kind = 2)`. The tests check:
  - the 20-team double round robin gives 380 matches, 10 per round, each ordered pair once;
  - the odd case skips byes;
  - composed with the captured Premier League team handles, its confirmed table and calendar, all 380 matches get a day over 38 distinct days, and no team plays twice on a day.

  Not yet replayed against the game. Which of `+0x14` and `+0x18` is home is also not established.
- **Probe ready** for the next ML creation: `tests/behaviour/cdb/schedule/` logs every Premier League match the game files under a day: day, record index, packed word, both team handles. One run turns the above into a cell-by-cell replay.

findings.title: RTTI vtable map of the 2021 exe (Track B)
findings.body:
`src/tools/rtti_map.py <exe> <out>` resolves MSVC x64 RTTI: type descriptor (`.?AV…`), complete object locator (signature 1, self-RVA), then the vtable after the qword that points to the locator. It scans only the non-executable sections under 64 MB; on this exe that takes 1 s and about 100 MB. Output, local only: `private-reference/rtti/vtables.tsv` and `virtuals.tsv`.

- Result: **11,029 classes, 13,461 locators and vtables (one each), 160,661 virtual slots, 30,023 distinct virtual functions**, 26,371 of them owned by a single class. The rest are shared bodies, presumably identical-code folding, so their class is ambiguous.
- Cross-check: 14 of our named functions are virtual, and the classes fit their independent names. Aoba's AI functions sit on `match::ai::ActionSelector…` classes (`GP_PullAwaySystem` on `ActionSelectorPullAway`, `DR_ParamSelection` on `ActionSelectorDiagonalRun`). `PES15_EngageDecision` is `match::player::ActionPress` slot 6, and `MatchControlUpdate` is `match::MatchControl` slot 1. **confirmed** that the map works. Each class attribution is **probable**, or a **guess** for shared bodies.
- New: the Master League regulation rebuild caller `0x141267040` (a skip row until now) is slot 2 of **`process::ModeDataCreationThread`**. It runs on the mode-data creation thread, which fits the worker-thread stacks of the regdrop probe.
- Use: look up `virtuals.tsv` before naming a function. A class plus slot is a strong naming hint. Not imported into the db, to avoid 30k automatic names; take names from it per batch.

findings.title: skeptic review of the fixture, calendar and ML-filter work (Track B/C)
league team counts come from the entry table (Track A/B)
findings.body:
The team-count difference for ids 82 and 30 is explained. For all 10 leagues checked, the setup's live count (RTE size) equals the number of `CompetitionEntry` rows for the regulation's competition in the update data:

| Regulation | League | File capacity | Entries | Live |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 82 | Italy D2 | 22 | 20 | 20 |
| 30 | Argentina D1 | 26 | 24 | 24 |
| 17, 79, 80, 116, 117, 134, 21, 118 | others | capacity = entries | | live = entries |

So the regulation's team field is a capacity, and the setup's team list holds the teams actually entered. **probable** (10/10 data match; the code that fills the setup's team list was not read).

Correction to earlier entries: regulation **117 is Switzerland** (10 × 4) and **134 is Scotland** (12 × 3). They were mislabelled above; fixed in place.

findings.title: Premier League schedule confirmed at run time; home slot still open (Track B/C)
findings.body:
One VM run with `tests/behaviour/cdb/schedule/`: a new Master League, the user's club Arsenal. Data: `tests/behaviour/competition/schedule_2026-11-03.txt`.

- **All 380 Premier League matches** that `Competition_Calendar_FileMatchOnDay` filed match the port exactly: creation order (record indices 0–379, so the match table was empty at that point), regulation 17 in the low word, round in bits 16–27, kind 2, both team handles at `+0x14`/`+0x18`, and the day from `match_day` on the big-league calendar. **confirmed**. The replay is in ctest `fixtures`. `league_matches` fidelity is raised to `exact`.
- `Match_GetTeamBySide` `0x140B00840` (169 callers) returns `+0x14 + side × 4`. So side 0 is `+0x14` and side 1 is `+0x18`.
- **Home slot: not settled.**
  - The user reports the first league game as **Arsenal (home) vs Manchester United**. In the capture, round 0's match with handle `0x19000C` pairs `+0x14 = 0x19000C` with `+0x18 = 0x1A0008`.
  - The two team identifications conflict. Taking `handle >> 14` as the team id, the 20 handles name 19 real 2020/21 clubs plus Bournemouth (4071), and **no Arsenal (101)**. `0x19000C` is then Manchester United (100) and `0x1A0008` is Leeds (104).
  - So either `handle >> 14` is not the file's team id (my team-name dump may be misread), or Master League swaps the user's club into another slot. **open**.
  - The two hypotheses give different Arsenal home/away sequences over league games 1–6. If `+0x18` is home (Arsenal = `0x1A0008`): H A H A H A, with game 2 against `0x1A800D`. If `+0x14` is home (Arsenal = `0x19000C`): H A H A A H, with game 2 against `0x330009`. The user's schedule screen settles it.

findings.title: league team handles are entry slots; a later draw is likely (Track B)
findings.body:
Correction and refinement of the previous entry.

- **Handle layout.** A team handle in the builder list and the match records is `team_id << 14 | entry slot`.
  - The Premier League's 20 `CompetitionEntry` rows (competition 9) hold slots 1–20 in alphabetical order. 19 of the 20 handles are exactly `file team id << 14 | slot`, for example `0x19000C` = Manchester United (100), slot 12 (0-based).
  - Slot 1 is Arsenal (101) in the file, but its handle is `0x3F9C0F1`: id 4071 with low bits 0xF1. The user's club is Arsenal, so this is probably Master League's copy of the user's club, a reserved id plus a marker. **probable**. So Arsenal is **not** missing; the previous entry's "no Arsenal" was a misreading. The same handle list appeared in two runs with Arsenal chosen.
- **Draw.** The captured schedule puts Arsenal's handle against Aston Villa's slot on day 233, and against Manchester United in rounds 11 (day 324) and 30. The user's screen shows Arsenal (home) vs Manchester United as the first league game. So the clubs that play are probably assigned to the slots after the schedule is built, by a draw, and the handles in the match records are placeholders at filing time. **guess**.
- **Next check (VM, no matches):** `tests/behaviour/cdb/schedule/main2.txt` (task `pesprobe5b`) dumps match records 0–379 (`+4`, `+0x14`, `+0x18`, `+8`) at the first day-step call (`0x1415120D0`, FootballLife) after creation. If the records then hold real clubs, the user's first fixture names the home slot directly.

findings.title: home slot is +0x14; handles are real clubs, no draw (Track B/C)
findings.body:
Second Master League creation (user's club Arsenal), probe v2 (`tests/behaviour/cdb/schedule/main2.txt`), then a non-invasive cdb read of the running game's match table (`tests/behaviour/cdb/schedule/champ.txt`). Data: `tests/behaviour/competition/champ_2026-11-04.txt`; the regulation-17 dump stayed in `private-reference/probes/`.

- **The Premier League records are identical to the 2026-11-03 run**: the same 380 (`+4`, `+0x14`, `+0x18`) triples. So the schedule is deterministic for a given setup. **confirmed** (two runs).
- **Handles name real clubs.** `handle >> 14` is the file team id. The Premier League list holds 19 clubs plus Bournemouth (4071, `0x3F9C0F1`), and **no Arsenal**. My 2026-11-03 reading of `0x3F9C0F1` as "Master League's copy of Arsenal" was wrong, and so was the "later draw" guess. Both are withdrawn. The low 14 bits are not the entry slot in general: Premier League clubs carry 1–19, Bournemouth 241, Championship clubs 239–259, and the user's Arsenal 0 (`0x194000`). Their meaning is open.
- **The user's club was moved to the Championship.** Arsenal plays regulation 79 (ENGLAND_D2_LEAGUE) and Bournemouth takes its Premier League place. Why is open (a Master League setup choice is the likely reason; not read). The 2026-11-03 report "first Premier League game Arsenal vs Manchester United" does not fit any captured record and is set aside.
- **Home is `+0x14` (side 0).** The user's screen against the records:

  | Match | `+0x14` | `+0x18` | Screen |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Championship round 1 | Arsenal | Millwall (387) | Arsenal home |
  | Championship round 2 | Preston (4192) | Arsenal | Arsenal away |
  | Championship round 3 | Arsenal | Birmingham (201) | Arsenal home |
  | England Cup (regulation 23) | Reading (391) | Arsenal | Reading home |

  4 of 4 agree. **confirmed** (runtime record plus UI). So `Match_GetTeamBySide` side 0 is home, and in `Competition_FixtureBuilder_EmitLeague` a row team whose cell flag is 1 plays away.
- Not yet replayed: the 24-team Championship through `league_matches` (needs the builder's team order for regulation 79).
- **Update (same day): the swap is not caused by the probe.** A third Master League, started without cdb (user's club Arsenal, chosen from the English League at setup), again put Arsenal in the 2nd Division. Its first league game was against Luton (4363), not Millwall, so the 2nd Division schedule differs between runs while the Premier League schedule did not. **confirmed** (user UI). The game data does not explain the swap. Our dt80 `CompetitionEntry` has Arsenal (101) in competition 9 and Bournemouth (4071) in competition 66 (slot 4). The VM has no EDIT save file, only `SYSTEM00000000`, and the same single update pack `dt80_100E_x64.cpk`. So the swap comes from Master League setup code, not from data. The code is not found yet. **probable**.

findings.title: the Master League setup moves the user's club down a division (Track B)
findings.body:
Probe `tests/behaviour/cdb/mlswap/` (VM task `pesprobe6`): at boot it finds the regulation-17 record and the dword holding Arsenal (`0x194000`, at record `+0x170`), then watches that dword with `ba w4`. The user created a new Master League with Arsenal. Log: `private-reference/probes/mlswap_2026-11-04.log`. The user's first league game was in the 2nd Division again, against Watford.

- **The swap write.** Write 15 stores `0x3F9C0F1` (Bournemouth) over Arsenal at `0x1414CA065`, inside `Competition_Regulation_SetTeamAt` `0x1414CA040`. That function writes `reg+0x170 + i×4` when `i < (reg+0x30A & 0x7F)`. Stack: `Competition_MLSetup_SwapUserClubDivision` `0x141262300` (return `0x1412627DF`), then `Competition_RegulationTable_RebuildFromList` `0x14126F7E0`, then `process::ModeDataCreationThread` slot 2 `0x141267040`.
