findings.title: behavioural CPU transfer model (Track C)
findings.body:
Commits e9ce6c6 to 9b5293a; report `docs/ml-audit-2026-11-16.md` ("After transfer model"), metrics tool `src/tools/transfer_metrics` with `docs/transfer-model-metrics.md`, audit metrics `tests/behaviour/audit/{before_transfer_model,after_players_moving,after_transfer_model}_cpu.tsv`, port rows `db/seeds/ports/transfer.tsv` (fidelity behavioural). The model is not a port of the game's search; it sits behind a plain-data World-in, Deals-out interface that an exact version can replace.

- **Game-evidenced (probable, decompiles of the CPU search plus dump counts):** a squad under 18 is topped up; the search counts the squad by registered position and fills a lacking group (under 4 defenders, 5 midfielders, 3 forwards, or no goalkeeper); loans return on 1 July and 1 January (probes 42 and 45); the 586 state-4 free records of 1 January leave by 21 February, 581 of them reset to age 16 and 474 of those at a club (probe 45 se8 to probe 46 dump 1). A "goalkeeper minimum of 3" is not the game's rule: the dumps show 60 to 92 clubs under 3 goalkeepers.
- **Ours, calibrated and labelled in the code:** squad size and buying weight by tier, seller limits, a goalkeeper minimum of 2, free-agent choice by rating and age, per-day deal counts (July from probe 42, August from probe 43), listing stock, and the winter window placed on 1 February (guess: no dump lies between 1 January and 21 February).
- **Bug found:** the day's listing flags (+0x14A bits 1 and 2) were never written back to the world, so listed players ran out within two windows and deals died out in later seasons. That, more than `kMinSquad`, caused the collapse.
- **Lineage note:** probe 43 is a different playthrough from probe 42 (968 club changes between 1 and 2 August), so the audit's summer 2021 totals mix two lineages.
- **Audit diff (CPU policy, 1 October, 2021 to 2025; game 2021 and 2022):** squad median 28/26/26/26/25 to 29 each year (game 29/28); clubs under 18 1/1/5/6/19 to 1 (game 0); free pool 1,581 to 4,889 becomes 1,105 to 1,189 (game 1,181 to 1,358); permanent moves 437/442/441/225/66 to 977 to 1,023 (game 1,057/1,134); new loans 209 to 10 becomes 540 to 565 (game 589/427); loan returns 300 to 369 (game 396/404); retirements at the switch 754 to 1,151 becomes 754 to 882 (game 758/816); overdue loans at 5 February 259/123/114/40 to 0; made-up free records about 160 a year to 0; players in two rosters and invalid loan owners to 0.
- **Open:** free signings are 76 to 112 a summer against the game's 254 and 390; clubs under 3 goalkeepers are 111 to 145 against 60 to 92; `owner_field_not_current_club` grows to 8,118 by 2025; 107 players in national-side matches with an empty roster in October 2025; the idle-user policy has only the one-season ctest; fees, search and negotiation are not modelled; the switch step draws about 1 in 5 regens as free; 2023 to 2025 have no game reference.

### Follow-up: free signings, goalkeepers, PlayerRecord +0x164

Commits e183a94 to 94e25f7. Full ctest with game data: 54 of 54, run after the last change.

- **Free signings were a measurement mismatch.** The game's 254 and 390 count from the 1 July dump, after the switch. The audit counted from before the switch, so records reset at the switch and then signed were counted as regens. Counted the same way (30 June to 26 September), the game shows 64 free signings plus 690 regens at a club, and the model 76 plus 711. Counted from the model's post-switch world, the model signs 309, 260 and 247 in 2021 to 2023.
- **Goalkeepers (ours, fitted).** Over July 2021 the game's clubs with 1/2/3/4/5 keepers go from 24/78/186/165/55 to 2/64/261/140/42, and 60 to 100 clubs stay at 2 all year. The decompiled "minimum 3" quota therefore does not bind in practice (probable). Rule: a club with one keeper buys one, a club with two does not buy a third, and no club sells its third. Clubs under 3 keepers at 1 October go from 111–145 to 60–79 (game 64–92).
- **PlayerRecord +0x164 (probable, seed added).** Deals and loan returns never change this field: in probe 42, none of 487 permanent movers, 238 loans, 159 free signings and 396 returns changed it. A reset record gets the club that keeps it: 465 of 465 at the 2021 switch, 411 of 474 in the winter window. The game's field goes stale by design. The model now sets it for placed regens, so mismatches at 1 October 2021 to 2025 go from 2,947–8,118 to 2,905–6,279 (game 2,868 in September 2021 and 4,073 in September 2022).
- **Open:** clubs with 6 or more keepers grow to 40 by 2025 (game 8 to 15); one `loan_owner_is_holder` failure in October 2024, probably a player loaned back to his parent club.

### Follow-up: keeper build-up, loaned players, national squads

Commits 87c9d7f to 2d4effc. Full ctest with game data: 54 of 54, run after the last code change. Metrics `tests/behaviour/audit/after_national_squads_cpu.tsv`.

- **A reset record keeps its registered position (probable).** It did so for 758 of 758 at the 2021 switch and 581 of 581 in the winter window (metric `reset.same_regpos`). The model's winter retirement step drew a new position, which piled keepers up. It now keeps the position. A regen goes to whichever of three random clubs has the fewest players in its position group; this placement rule is ours, as the game's is unread. Clubs with 6 or more keepers at 1 October 2021 to 2025 now number 10/14/18/18/15 (game 8 to 15).
- **Loaned players do not move on (probable from counts).** Of 1,195 new loans in probes 42, 43 and 45 to 49, none goes to the owner. Of about 3,000 moves of any kind, none moves a player who was on loan. The model now neither sells nor loans out a player on loan (`Player::on_loan`; the rule is ours, the counts are the evidence). `loan_owner_is_holder` and `loan_owner_invalid` are 0 at every checkpoint.
- **National squads are static across the dumps (probable).** The 102 national sides hold the same 2,346 entries in every dump of probes 38, 42, 45, 47 and 49, across the 1 July switch too. A reset record stays in its squad, and the dumps show no call-up step. The model's switch and loan-return steps had removed reset or moved records from every roster, which left national sides empty. They now edit club squads only, and all 102 national sides keep 11 or more players. Exhibition squads now never change; in the game, 19 of their 23 players are the same in 2022.
- **Audit at 1 October 2021 to 2025 (keeper round):** permanent moves 959 to 996 (game about 1,057 and 1,134), new loans 564 to 576 (game 589 and 427), squad median 29, no club under 18, free pool 1,076 to 1,189 (game 1,181 to 1,358).

findings.title: Chilean playoffs, Libertadores cup winners, idle-user five seasons (Track C)
findings.body:
Commits d08ace2 to 9a6b664. Full ctest with game data: 54 of 54, run after the last change. Seeds: 693 cited, 0 gaps.

- **Regs 160 and 161 (Chilean playoffs, probable).** Reg 119 (20 clubs) has two parts, 168 (21 January to 2 May) and 169 (26 July to 7 November). Each playoff holds 14 records: reg 160 runs 13 May to 24 June and reg 161 runs 18 November to 12 December. Its list is the top 8 of the part's final table in the order 1, 5, 4, 8, 2, 6, 3, 7 (3 of 3 captures). Consecutive pairs make the two-legged quarter-finals, with the higher seed at home first. The playoff is filed on the day the part's last match is played, like the promotion playoffs. That creation day is inferred from the dates.
- **Reg 160's dates are a static table, confirmed.** 0x142990B80 holds 8 `{day, round, flags}` rows, read as case 0xA0 of the date function 0x14157F810 (seed `Competition_Calendar_DatesCase56_Reg160`). `ml_year_build` block C strips each playoff from the game's dump and refiles it. All 14 records match in round, date and quarter-final sides, and in slot for 2 of 3 captures. The 2021 reg 160 is compared without slots, because other regulations held the lower slots when it was filed.
- **A cup winner who already holds a place (probable, no capture of the case).** Targets 8 and 9 give the place to the league's next club, as the 2026-11-08 entry describes. The Argentine league used is the aggregate reg 51 (period 6), which is inferred. This fixes the December Libertadores list, which held 7 of 8 when the Copa Argentina winner (reg 54) was already qualified; it now holds 8 of 8 in 2021 to 2024. With the CPU policy and strict families the audit reports 0 family failures (3 before). The CL qualifiers' duplicate rule (targets 2 and 3) is still unknown, so nothing is replaced there.
- **Idle-user policy over five seasons** (`PES_AUDIT_USER=idle`, about 3.5 minutes; metrics `after_libertadores_replace_idle.tsv`). It crashed in summer 2024: nobody runs the user's club, so it had one player and no lineup, and `goal_events` read an empty vector. A side with no lineup now scores without scorers (`match_day_test`). The run then completes 925 steps with 0 family and 0 list failures. Transfers, loans, squads, the free pool and retirements agree with the CPU policy within generator noise. The only real difference is the idle club itself, which falls under 18 and then under 11 players from 2023; this is expected, as nobody renews or signs for it.
- `ml_season`'s free-run `playoffs_created` count now includes the Chilean playoffs: 2 to 3 in season 1 and 2 to 4 in season 2. Its record-equality checks are unchanged.
- **Open:** reg 131 has no list rule; the CL qualifiers' duplicate rule is unknown; the 1 February winter-window date is a guess; fees, the search and negotiation are not modelled.

findings.title: probe 51, the winter window is daily through January (Track B runtime, Track C model)
findings.body:
Probe 51 ran on the season 2 lineage, from late August 2022 to early March 2023. It used four low-rate hardware breakpoints: MatchSim_RunDay (dumps), TransferManager_HandleMessage 0x140F132A0 (deal messages with the ML date), MLTransfer_Player_AddToTeam 0x140F13E90 and RemoveFromTeam 0x140F142B0. The data is in `private-reference/probe51/` (`run51.log` and 12 dumps taken on 19 December 2022, then 1, 2, 8, 15, 22 and 29 January, and 1, 4, 11, 16 and 24 February 2023). The scripts are `tests/behaviour/cdb/mlswap/*51.txt`, and the analysis is `src/tools/analysis/winter51.py`. Model commits cdb8ecb and cd6f6c3.

- **Timing (confirmed, runtime log; this replaces the 1 February guess):**
  - 31 December: 324 loan returns (message 0x10C000D) and 531 messages 0x10C0010 from `Retirement_PostPlayerLeaves`, one for each winter-flagged club player.
  - 1 January: 462 deals (0x10C0007). 443 of them have no source club, which are the leavers' placements; the rest are 14 permanent moves and 5 loans.
  - 2 to 31 January: 8 to 32 deals a day, 244 permanent, 205 loans and 72 free signings. There are no free signings on 2 to 6, 30 or 31 January.
  - 31 January: 41 messages 0x10C000F (`TransferManager_OnContractExpired`, now probable).
  - Nothing after 31 January except one message on 21 February.
  - Every signed record is at its destination club in the next dump (1,100 of 1,100).
- **Summer deadline:** 31 August 2022 has 96 deals (71 permanent, 20 loans, 5 free) and 70 contract expiries. Probe 43 (2021) showed no deals on 31 August, so the deadline-day volume varies by season or by lineage.
- **Winter leavers (probable, dumps):** state-4 free records are reset the same step, not by late February. The 1 January dump holds 8 against 22 on 19 December. 546 records were reset to age 16 between the dumps of 19 December and 1 January (531 leavers plus about 15 state-4 records). Of the 531 leavers, 384 stay at their club (72%), 35 go to another club, 104 stay free and 8 are not reset. Probe 45's 586 state-4 records were this step caught mid-way. This corrects the 1 February retirement step of the earlier entries.
- **Model (behavioural):**
  - January runs as a daily window, using probe 51's per-day arrays.
  - The 1 January step has about 15 permanent moves, 6 loans and 15 free signings.
  - Leavers are reset on 2 January with the exact `regen_reset`, keeping their position. 72% stay at their club, 7% go to another club (our placement), and the rest stay free.
  - The reset is a day late so that `ml_consistency`'s comparison with probe 45's mid-step dump still holds.
  - Over 2 to 31 January the model makes 241 permanent moves (game 244), 204 loans (game 205) and 136 free signings (game 72).
  - Full ctest with game data: 54 of 54.
- **Open:**
  - January free signings are too high in the model, coming from our squad-need refills.
  - Resets per winter fall each year (616 to 414), and the 1 October free pool drifts to 931 by 2025.
  - The model has no 31 August deadline deals.
  - Contract expiry happens on the month turn in the model, one day after the game's 31 January and 31 August.

### Follow-up: contract months, winter refills, the 31 August passes

Commits ae0e488 to 6a9a8a9. Full ctest with game data: 54 of 54.

- **Contract expiry day (probable, dumps).** Each message carries the date being processed, and the next dump shows the state after it. The 41 players expiring on 31 January 2023 hold month-1 contracts in the 29 January dump. In the 1 February dump they are clubless with the contract cleared, so the model's month-turn step already removes them at the same step. Releases between 20 December and 5 February are still low in the model: 26 to 6, against the game's 41 (2023) and 62 (2021/22).
- **Contract month follows the buying club (ours, from counts).** About 40% of club players hold month-1 contracts, and that share is stable: 6,356 on 30 June 2021, 6,319 in July 2022 and 6,442 on 1 January 2023. 406 of the 435 regens placed on 1 January 2023 hold month 1, against 30 of 496 placed on 1 July 2022. Among the July and August 2021 movers, month 1 is 147 of 487 permanent moves, 75 of 238 loans and 64 of 159 free signings. The model gave every signing month 8, which shrank the month-1 population and with it the winter retirement flags. A signing now takes the contract month most common at the buying club. With this, winter resets run 616, 588, 571 and 523, against 546 in the game; flagged club players run 598 to 501, against 562 and 531 in the game; and the 1 October free pool runs 1,037 to 1,186.
- **Winter refills** now skip the days on which the game signs nobody. The audit's free signings from 20 December to 5 February run 49 to 73, against the game's 72 plus 24 on 1 January. The earlier 136 came from the unswitched March 2021 test world, whose squads are thin.
- **The daily deal step runs once per `MatchSim_RunDay` pass (probable).** Probe 51's 96 deals on 31 August 2022 come from six passes on that date: the DAY line for day 242 repeats five times, with 8 to 25 deals per pass. Probe 43 had one pass per day and no deals on 31 August. This is not a deadline spike, so it is not modelled.
- **Open:** winter releases are low; month-1 contracts are signed with the same year as month-8 ones, whereas the game's switch regens add a year.

findings.title: 20-season stress test; the ML calendar has no 29 February (Track B static, Track C)
findings.body:
Commits 77d2e4a to be3095e (stress test) and 40beb0e to 0f9c052 (fixes). The report is in `docs/ml-audit-2026-11-16.md`, sections "20-season stress test" and "After fixes". The runs are `tests/behaviour/audit/stress20_*{,_v2}.tsv`, analysed with `src/tools/stress_report.py`. The audit gained `PES_AUDIT_SEED` and player-record capacity metrics. Full ctest with game data: 55 of 55.

- **Stress test, before fixes.** Four 20-season runs: cpu with the default seed, cpu with seed 20261117, idle, and cpu from probe 51 dump 12. None crashed, none had an invalid reference, and none ran out of record slots (17,289 slots, all used, none created or lost). 12 of the 13 family failures per run came from the leap-year calendar, and the free pool collapsed from about 1,150 to 70–85.
- **The ML calendar has 365 day indexes every year (probable, code only).**
  - `Date_MonthTable` 0x142979940 holds 12 triples {month, first index, last index}. February runs 31 to 58 and December ends at 364.
  - `Date_ToDayIndex` 0x1414C90F0 and `Date_FromYearDay` 0x1414C9270 convert through it. `Competition_MLSetup_BuildRankings` 0x1412695B0 stores the day word (+0x1642A1C), the year (+0x1642A1E) and the date (+0x1642A24) through them.
  - Every inline date add found uses February = 28 and the 30-day-month mask 0xA50, with no leap rule: 111 loads in 86 functions, including two in `ML_DayStep_Outer` 0x1413007D0.
  - The routine that advances the day word each ML day was not found in plain code, so this is "probable", not "confirmed". The dumps (2020 to 2023) hold no 29 February.
  - The engine now uses 365-day years: 28 February 2024 is index 58, 1 March is 59 and 31 December is 364. The `ml_calendar` test checks all 365 days of 2023 to 2025 against the transcribed conversions. The leap-year 31 December build is reached by the normal day sequence, with no catch-up.
- **Free pool (cause probable, fixes ours).**
  - In 2021 and 2022 the model's pool flows match the game's dumps: winter leavers 562 against 531, placed regens 447 against 443, and 1 September expiries 136/74 against 151/92.
  - Free signings ran at about 385 a year whatever the pool size, while the expiry inflow shrank (136, 74, 47, 28, 20) as the near-term contract cohorts emptied. Contract lengths do not drift (mean 2.94 to 2.99, game 2.95).
  - CPU renewals run 8 to 15% above the game's counts. Correcting that alone did not stop the fall, so it is not in.
  - **Calibrated (our fixes):**
    - free signings go only to a club with a need, and never into a squad of 40;
    - a daily free signing succeeds with probability pool/1,230 while the pool is under 1,230 (the game's five-dump mean);
    - a club with 5 keepers buys no more keepers.

    This is a labelled approximation of a mechanism not yet read (probably the cached club plan keeping the near-term contract cohorts full).
  - **Effect:** the pool now stays at 804 to 1,184 in all runs and is flat after season 14. That is still about 300 below the game's 1,181 to 1,358. Clubs with 6 or more keepers number 6 to 13 (game 8 to 15).
- **World Cup 2026 (class b: entrants not generated).**
  - It is scheduled: include key 10 of regs 34 and 35 gives 5 August 2025, and the step is reached.
  - Our `done` guard stays set because the 2022 records are never freed. The entrants would still be the 2022 cycle's, since the build of the qualifier regulations 36 to 40 (include key 11, 5 August 2024) has no model code and has not been read.
  - Lifting the guard alone would file a wrong tournament, so it is left open.
- **After fixes:** each run has 1 family failure (World Cup 2026); every other season and calendar family is `ok` in all years. Mean rating (68.8 to 65.2), age and wage still drift, with no game reference after 2023.
- **Open:** the key-11 qualifier build; what keeps the game's near-term contract cohorts full; the day-advance routine; `club_starter_slot_invalid_or_duplicate` (3 to 94); the `slots_empty_t*` duplicate-place shortcut; idle-user club decay.

### Follow-up: World Cup qualifiers (include key 11) ported

Commit a292e55. New ctest `ml_wc_qual`. Seeds: 697 cited, 0 gaps. Full ctest with game data: 56 of 56. This replaces the open "World Cup 2026" item above.

- **Verified game algorithm (read, ported, equal to the probe 38 dump of the 2020 step):**
  - `ML_StepC` 0x141366070 runs 0x14135E760 for each of regs 36 to 40 on include key 11.
  - The event table 0x14298CA30 puts key 11 on day 216 of years 2020, 2024, 2028 and so on, which is 5 August. The include table is 0x14298CB60.
  - The entrant picker 0x141556200 takes each regulation's entry key (0x14150C930: keys 0, 2, 3, 4, 1) and drops sides with fewer than 11 squad players. It puts user sides first, then the rest by national ranking, up to N = +0x30C & 0x7F (32, 6, 10, 10, 10).
  - The pot draw 0x1415299B0 uses G = +0x307 & 0x3F groups. It sorts by ranking into pots of G, shuffles each pot and deals one side from each pot to each group. 0x141545F00 slices the list equally into the child groups.
  - FillEntrantLists frees every record of the key's regulations, and RegisterAll files them into the lowest free slots.
  - Date cases 12 to 15 are at 0x14298E480, 0x14298E4D0, 0x14298E550 and 0x14298E630.
  - **Comparison with the dump:** entrant sets 5 of 5, pots 30 of 30, group lists 14 of 14 (given the game's master lists), records 296 of 296 equal in slot, round, date and sides.
- **Freeing the previous tournament on the key-10 step (probable):** the same mechanism as the 1 January purge. No capture has an earlier tournament present on 5 August. This removes our `done` guard defect.
- **Matches observed behaviour only:** the order inside a pot comes from our generator's draw, because no capture holds the game's 2020 draw. The national ranking is the dump's and is never updated.
- **Inferred:**
  - A date day before 216 falls in the year after the build; the dump fits any threshold from 204 to 243.
  - The +0x424 squad count is read as the roster size.
- **Audit:** the 20-season cpu run has 0 family failures. The World Cup is ok in 2022, 2026, 2030, 2034 and 2038, and its qualifiers in 2020, 2024 and so on. The other three 20-season runs were not repeated. Beyond 2023 this only checks that the competitions exist and are played.
- **Open:** keys 12 and 13 (regs 0x29, 0x2C, 0x2E, 0x68: the Euro and other tournaments); the early BuildGroups caller 0x14135F0B0, not read to the end; the club-rank and value-sort branches of the pot draw.

### Follow-up: rating drift (Track C model, Track B dump reads)

Commits 46d34ac (metrics and the `rating_drift` dump tool), 55d009d (1 January development, rating-weighted retirement flag), 3d97c3b (docs/ml-audit-2026-11-16.md "Rating drift: cause and fix", `stress20_cpu_seed0_v4.tsv`). New ctest `winter_development`. Full ctest with game data: 57 of 57. Seeds: 708 cited, 0 gaps; no new game address is cited.

- **Cause, matches observed behaviour:** the game develops players twice a year, at the season switch and again on 1 January. The model ran only the switch step.
  - The same-player year change in the dumps (age 16 +1.70, 20 +2.09, 24 +0.83, 30 -1.28) is about twice the switch step alone.
  - Probe 51 dump 1 (19 Dec 2022) to dump 2 shows +0.85 up to age 21 and -0.8 at 31 and over. The other dump pairs inside a season (Jul to Sep 2021, Sep 2021 to Jan 2022, Mar to Jun 2022) show 0.00.
  - With the age after the 1 January ageing, 16,646 of 16,668 eligible records have all 25 abilities inside the two outcomes of the existing development rule; with the age before it, 14,675.
  - Not found: the caller of the 1 January step and its draw order (ours), and the rule for the 531 players already flagged for retirement (their abilities fall about 5; the model leaves them untouched).
- **Retirement flag by rating, only our fit (level 3):** flagged club players of age 27 to 32 are 2 to 4 points below others of their age in two 30 June dumps. `RetireScale` weights the flag probability by rating and keeps the counts by age. Effect about 0.05 a year on the mean. The game's real flag rule is not read.
- **Not causes:** the regen reset and the switch development are the ported game algorithms (2026-11-13) and match the dumps by age (age 20 / 25 / 30 / 35: game 1.18 / 0.32 / -0.40 / -0.66, model 1.23 / 0.33 / -0.42 / -0.66 in 2021). Retiree counts match (757 to 816 a year). Growth and potential words do not change between dumps for records that are not reset.
- **Game against model, 2022 (matches observed behaviour):** club players on 30 June 15,005 / 68.74 against 15,185 / 68.56; starters 71.70 against 71.60; ages 22 to 28 after the switch 69.61 against 69.51; same-player year change of club players +0.18 against +0.16.
- **20 seasons, cpu seed 0 (level 3, no reference after 2023):** mean club rating at 1 July for seasons 1 / 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 was 68.96 / 67.17 / 65.57 / 65.43 / 65.17 and is now 68.96 / 67.72 / 67.95 / 69.90 / 69.85. Mean age is unchanged. The dip near season 6 comes from the dump's small 16 to 18 cohort (113 players) moving up the bands. The later rise to about 70 comes from regens inheriting their retirees' potential (72.5 in the dumps, against 70.5 for the dump's 22 to 28 players); this uses the game's own reset rule, but no dump can confirm the long-run outcome. Wages rise to 6,053 by season 20 (2,472 before). Strict run: 0 family failures. `club_roster_above_40` appears in 5 snapshots.
- **Open:** the flag rule; the 1 January decline of flagged players; the exe caller of the 1 January step; the other three 20-season runs; wage growth under the fees model.

findings.title: CPU clubs have no money; fees and budgets are ours; movers take the wage rule (Track B dumps, Track C model)
findings.body:
Commits 9e6e2ef (`src/game/transfer/club_money.{h,cpp}`, wage at deal, tests `club_money` and `mover_wage`) and d93a056 (audit money metrics, `tests/behaviour/audit/stress20_cpu_seed0_v5.tsv`). Full ctest with game data: 59 of 59.

- **No CPU club money (probable):**
  - Over probe 42 dumps 8 to 39 (8 July to 8 August 2021), 581 teams changed roster. No team-record word tracks the deals; only the roster, its derived arrays and the ratings at team +0x400 to +0x41C follow them.
  - Outside the team records, the only money words that move are the user's block (+0x16ECBF4, +0x16ECC08, +0x16ECC10) and the user squad array at +0x16EE85C (stride 0x34, guess).
  - The deal executors 0x140F15770, 0x140F13A40 and 0x140F14770 call no finance code. `Finance_OnTransferMoneyA`/`B` (0x140F7A710, 0x140F7ADA0) change only the owner's own finance block.
  - Not checked: heap objects outside EditData, and every caller path.
- **Wage at a deal (matches observed behaviour):**
  - A permanent mover or free signing takes the confirmed wage rule (`player_value`, src/game/ml/finance.cpp) at the new club. Loanees keep their wage.
  - July 2021 (probe 42): movers 473 of 487, free signings 158 of 159, loanees 238 of 238 unchanged.
  - January 2023 (probe 51): movers 186 of 214 (28 unexplained), free signings 71 of 72, loanees 181 of 181.
  - Wages change at no other time inside a window.
- **PlayerRecord +0x174 market value (still guess):**
  - It never changes with a move (0 of 812 movers, 0 of 76 free signings) and is 0 for 40% of club players.
  - Median non-zero value by rating: 64 is 1,500; 70 is 6,500; 76 is 40,000; 82 is 240,000; 88 is 640,000. Units are not proven.
- **Fees and budgets (only ours, level 3):**
  - A permanent deal pays a log-linear value by rating, less 12% a year over age 30.
  - Club budgets come from 1.5 to 2 years of income, scaled from the user's 0.92% monthly share. A buyer only considers sellers it can afford.
  - Fees and budgets sit behind `World::use_budgets`, which only `ml_day` turns on. The game has no counterpart, so this constraint is not game behaviour.
  - Summer permanent deals fall from 1,006 to 965 (the game had 1,057 and 1,134).
- **20 seasons, cpu seed 0, v5 against v4 (level 3):**
  - Ratings, squads and deal counts are within about 1% of v4. Wage mean at the end is 6,164 against 6,053.
  - The rich-to-poor club rating gap falls from 9.4 to 6.3.

### Follow-up: 20-season stress test v6, CPU budgets off

Commit 169ac70 makes CPU club budgets an option, off by default (`ml::World::cpu_club_budgets`), on the user's decision to keep the model accurate. The four 20-season runs (docs/ml-audit-2026-11-16.md, "20-season stress test v6") have no abort and every competition family `ok`. Transfers are stable (summer permanent 965 to 1,048, squad median 28 to 29), so no transfer imbalance calls for the club-plan probe. Open: an idle user club falls below 11 players from season 3; the population ages younger (mean 26.8 to 24.7, retirements 770 to 560), probably because the start dump is not a stationary population (level 3, no reference after 2023).

findings.title: lineup slot map kept in step with the squad (Track B read, Track C fix)
findings.body:
Commits 5c86e28, 91ac471, 279e6f7, ff7a66b. New `src/game/ml/squad.h` (`roster_remove`, `roster_add`, `set_starters`), ctest `squad`. Full ctest 60 of 60. The audit invariant `club_starter_slot_invalid_or_duplicate` is 0 in every snapshot of a 5-season cpu run (it was 1 to 102 before). In the game's dumps it is 0 of 555 clubs in probes 38, 42 and 51, so the earlier counts were malformed model data, not a faulty check.

- **Verified game algorithm (read and ported):** `Team_Squad_RemovePlayer` 0x1415720D0 calls `Team_Squad_RemoveRef` 0x141268AE0, which finds the squad index k, shifts every later ref (and the u16 list at +0x29A) down one and decrements the count. With flag 1 (the transfer path) it then sets the formation slot equal to k (+0x220, 40 bytes) to 0xFF and lowers every slot entry above k by one; the role bytes +0x248 to +0x251 are renumbered the same way.
- **Matches observed behaviour:** probe 42 (38 daily pairs, July 2021): 456 of 459 clubs that only lost bench players, and 262 of 264 that lost one starter, have exactly the renumbered map with the bench closed up and one bench entry moved into the vacated slot. Probe 51 (January 2023) gives 129 of 302 and 52 of 102, with CPU matches and the 1 January switch between dumps. Every game slot map is a permutation of its roster (555 of 555 in two dumps).
- **Read, not ported:** with more than 10 players left the removal calls `Team_AutoSelectLineup` in context mode 1 (`Lineup_Context_Init` 0x141504050, guess), which refills the empty starter slot; its scoring is not read (the filler is the first bench entry in only 49 of 314 cases). `Team_Squad_AddPlayer` 0x141571EC0 appends the ref and then rebuilds the lineup (mode 3 for transfers, guess; 0 of 860 add-only clubs kept their old map).
- **Only ours:** the refill takes the first bench entry not in the XI; an added player takes the first free slot after the bench; `set_starters` keeps the bench order. The real source of the duplicates was the CPU-match write of the XI into slots 0 to 10 without fixing the bench.
- **Effect on the audit:** deal counts stay in their band; February contract releases rise (22, 14, 17, 11 to 39, 34, 18, 19), probably because renewal reads the XI through the slots. Not checked.
- **Open:** port the mode-3 rebuild on add (already ported for matches in `match_day.h`); the 1 January switch roster order (172 clubs in probe 51 dumps 1 to 2); `Team::squad` raw refs are not updated by the helpers.

findings.title: continental slot picks, the taken-club rule read (Track B read, Track C port)
findings.body:
The model left a CL or CL-qualifier slot row empty when its club was already placed and let pool key 69 fill the hole (the "duplicate-place shortcut", docs/todo.md item 2). The game's rule is now read and ported. Code: `src/game/ml/continental_next.cpp` `picks_for`, `src/game/ml/season_build.cpp` (holders). Seeds `db/seeds/slots1.tsv`, two data rows, three port rows.

- **Verified game algorithm (read):** `Competition_NextList_SlotPicks` 0x1413561F0 walks the leagues of the confederation (period 1, 6 or 11, +0x304 top bits 01) and calls `Competition_NextList_FinalTablePicks` 0x141356BA0 per league country. That builds the placed list (`Competition_NextList_PlacedTeams` 0x141351BC0: the new reg 3, 2 and 5 lists for Europe; 9 and 8 for South America; 15 for Asia) and runs the pick object (vtable 0x1428EF1F8) through `Competition_Table_VirtualPick` 0x1413B83A0:
  - `+0x18` 0x1413B7B50: the country's slot rows (table 0x1434F1FA0, a byte-identical copy of 0x1434EECC0) in table order. A free club is added. A taken club: a cup-winner row (period 2, 16 or 17, `FUN_1414CF180`) takes the cup's runner-up when free; otherwise the row adds 1 to the country's count. A row with no club (league too short) adds nothing.
  - `+0x28` 0x1413B80A0 (disassembly 0x1413B80DF to 0x1413B8208; Ghidra drops these blocks as unreachable): walks the country's league standings (`FUN_1413B7910`) and appends the first clubs not yet picked or placed, one per count.
  - `Competition_NextList_Helper571C0` 0x1413571C0, Europe only, at the end of a list: qual type 0 (reg 3) adds the CL winner when absent, else the EL winner when absent; qual type 1 (reg 2) adds the EL winner when no list holds it. The holder rows (reg 4 and 6, position 0) are never slot rows, since no league has their country.
  - `Competition_NextList_BuildByKind` 0x141355C90 then fills from pool key 0x45 (69) and trims to 24 / 16 / 40 (qual types 0 / 1 / 2), which is the model's existing top-up. `Competition_QualType_ToRegulation` 0x1413535E0 maps 0, 1 and 2 to regs 3, 2 and 5.
- **Matches observed behaviour (game references, ml_consistency with `PES_BUILD=1`):**
  - Probes 42 and 48 (2021 switch): reg 5 had 3 wrong clubs; it now equals the game's list, 40 of 40 in order. Reg 2 and reg 3 unchanged (reg 2 equal as a set; the order is the draw's).
  - Probe 47 (2022 switch, two pairs): reg 5 had 6 wrong clubs; now 2. The 8 cup runner-up picks (100, 366, 112, 234, 273, 1957, 1985, 2070) are all in the game's list. Misses: 5191 and 1195 change places between reg 2 and reg 5 (reg 115's places 2 and 3 in the model's table; also before this change, probable tie-break); and the model has 2067 (reg 141's place 3 in the model's table) where the game has 1208, which the old model held only through the pool. Cause of the second not established.
- **Only ours or unverified:**
  - The country fill uses the lowest-id period 1/6 league of the area (11 too at the July build); the game takes the last flagged league in its country list. They agree on every case seen.
  - An unfinished cup's row is still served from the league's next free place (fitted 2026-11-08; the game's incomplete branch `Helper57470` is not read).
  - The Libertadores and AFC lists use the same pick code and now follow the same rule; `ml_continental_next` (reg 9 28 of 28 in order, AFC 32 of 32) still passes.
- **Metric change:** the audit's `slots_empty_t*` now counts only rows that stay empty (it also counted rows served later).
- **Unresolved (not reconstructed; the port is behavioural, not exact):**
  - Probe 47 EL / CL-qualifier lists still differ from the game in 2 clubs: 5191 and 1195 swapped between reg 2 and reg 5 (probably reg 115's tie-break, unproven), and 2067 in place of 1208 (cause unknown; whether 1208 is reg 141's place 3 in the game was not checked).
  - The game's incomplete-league branch (`Helper57470`) and the country-fill league choice (last flagged league) are not ported; the model's substitutes are fitted.
  - The Libertadores and AFC lists were not re-checked against a game reference beyond the existing `ml_continental_next` assertions.

findings.title: team membership fields of the player record (Track B read, dumps)
findings.body:
Full analysis: `docs/state-duplication-findings-2026-11-18.md`. Seeds updated (`db/seeds/slots1.tsv`, `db/seeds/competition1.tsv`). No model change yet.

- **Recovered algorithm (read):**
  - `Player_SetTeamSlot` 0x1414C04D0 writes a team handle into PlayerRecord +0x12C + 4k, for slot k < 3.
  - `MLTransfer_Player_RemoveFromTeam` 0x140F142B0 removes the player from the squad of the team in slot 0, writes +0x160 = that team, clears +0x148 bits 17-18 and sets slot 0 invalid.
  - `MLTransfer_Player_AddToTeam` 0x140F13E90, with no destination: state 2 and slot 0 invalid. Otherwise: `Team_Squad_AddPlayer`, state 0, wage and contract from the deal, then slot 0 = the destination (for a loan, the holding club).
- **Matches observed behaviour (six dumps, probes 42, 45, 47, 51):**
  - +0x12C is the club whose squad holds the player for every rostered club player, including loanees (about 16,000 per dump), and invalid for every clubless record (states 1 to 4).
  - +0x130 is the national side when the player is in a national squad.
  - The squad ref's high dword is the record's +0x30 id (18,437 of 18,437 refs).
  - A record reset at the season switch keeps its +0x30 id (758 of 758 in 2021, 816 of 816 in 2022).
- **Model state (only ours):**
  - `Player::team0` and `Team::squad` are written by the loader only. In the five-season run they differ from the roster for up to 6,647 players and 555 clubs.
  - `Player::morale`'s packed copy is skipped by the CPU post-match morale pass (`ml_day.cpp:933`); nothing reads that copy.

findings.title: one storage for the squad list; the winter renewal reads the real squads (Track C model fix, Track B read)
findings.body:
Fixes from the 2026-11-18 entry, one commit each: the CPU post-match morale pass writes the packed +0x13C copy (7069b96); club roster changes keep `Player::team0` (+0x12C) as `MLTransfer_Player_AddToTeam` / `RemoveFromTeam` do (6653d30); `Team::squad` is removed and the squad refs are formed from the roster and the record's +0x30 id (`squad_ref`, fix 3). Investigation logs: `private-reference/remediation/fix3_investigation/REPORT.md`.

- **Representation (matches observed, seven dumps):** the loader builds the roster from the +0x14C refs in order; the game's ref is index | (+0x30) << 32 on 127,450 of 127,450 refs (probes 38, 42 x2, 45, 47, 49, 51). `squad_ref` returns the compact index | id << 16 that `Team::squad` held, so the start-of-run `team_squad` hash is unchanged.
- **Old-model defects, confirmed (probe 45, 1 January 2022 step, old and new code on the same dump):** in 70 of 554 clubs the old renewal read the stale loaded list because its count equalled the roster size. Effects: 20 flagged leavers, clubless with contract 0, were renewed (the game renewed 0 of 20: all clubless, contract 0); loan returnees were visited at the borrower as well as, or instead of, the owner; the stale list order was paired with a slot map renumbered for the roster, so starters, squad average and tiers came from the wrong players.
- **Measured against the game (probe 45 dump 21):** the change alters 122 renewal decisions (87 removed, 35 added). The new model agrees with the game on 98 of 122, the old one on 24. The renewal count moves from 4,300 to 4,248 (game 3,986). The 24 remaining disagreements (13 stale-club removals the game did renew, 8 loan-returnee renewals the game did not make, 2 loan-returnee removals the game did renew, 1 stale-club addition) are **not individually explained**.
- **Moves 498 to 497 (game 500):** 20 players move only in the old run and 19 only in the new; none of the 39 is among the 122 changed renewals and the game moved none of them. A downstream effect of the changed contracts, wages and draws, not a direct one (probable).
- **Unresolved: the order inside the 1 January step.** The model runs loan returns, then flagged leavers, then `ComAgent_RenewContracts`. The mid-step dump `edit45_se8` already holds all three (477 returns, 566 leavers, 3,986 renewals), so the dumps cannot order them. Read so far: `ML_DayStep_Outer` 0x1413007D0 calls `MLDay_Players_ClearStatusBits45` 0x14156BE90 (clears +0x13C bits 4-5 only) on event 3 or 6, then `MLMode_DailyComponentsStep` 0x140F67630, which runs `ComAgent_DailyWork`. `MLTransfer_LoanReturns_Run` 0x140F17730 has one static caller, `MLSetup_TransferSteps_Run` 0x140F68300, reached from `Competition_MLSetup_Run` 0x141267040 through data references only. Where the January returns and leavers run relative to the daily work is not read.
- **Unresolved: the contract tier.** The over-renewal (4,248 against 3,986) stays attributed to nothing proven; the cached club plan (2026-11-14 entry) is a candidate, not an explanation.
- Verification: full ctest with data, five-season seed-0 audit and per-component world/RNG snapshots against the pre-fix baseline; components identical through the 2021 season build, divergence from the 1 January 2022 step.

findings.title: order of the 1 July and 1 January transitions (Track B evidence, Track C comparison)
findings.body:
Full write-up: `docs/ml-step-order-investigation-2026-11-19.md`. Read-only; no model change.

- **Discriminator (observed):** `ComAgent_RenewContracts` 0x140F283B0 prices a renewed player at the club whose squad it walks. Loanees that stay on loan and are renewed get the borrower's wage whenever the borrower's and owner's differ (1 January 129 to 0, 1 July 34 to 0; probes 45 and 48). So a loan returnee's renewal wage shows where the renewal met him.
- **1 January (probe 45 dump 20 to se8):** 122 renewed returnees carry the owner's wage (109 owner only, 0 borrower only, 10 both, 3 neither): **loan returns run before the renewals (observed)**, as the model does. The leavers' position against the renewals is not determinable from these dumps (flagged players are skipped either way; no flagged loanee returned). No draw log covers this step.
- **1 July (probe 48 day-180 step):** loan returns also run before the renewals (90 owner only, 0 borrower only of 124). The draw log orders the drawing parts: daily blocks, renewals (0x140F28759 from draw 636), the CPU agents' search, finance (0x14133D717, 0x14133D778), the build (0x14152CD70 from draw 148,665), the season development (0x1412DD6E6 from draw 161,406), then the retiree reset and youth path. No block draws the winter retirement flags.
- **Confirmed differences from the model's switch (observed):** the model renews before the loan returns; it develops and resets retirees before the build; its switch-day deals come after development, not right after the renewals. Hypothesis: the game's build keys are the post-transfer, pre-development squads (the model takes them before the switch). The model rolls the winter flags with draws inside the switch; the game does not on this step, and where it sets them is unresolved.
- **Proposed, not applied:** loan returns before renewals; the build between the pre-build part of the switch (returns, renewals, deals, finance) and the post-build part (development, retirement, regens), with keys taken at build time. Both change the generator stream and every baseline after the first switch.

### 2026-11-19: correction C1, July loan returns before the renewals (Track C)

What changed: `run_season_switch` returns the loans ending 30 June before the CPU renewals, as the game does (entry above). The block itself and every other part of the switch are unchanged.

- **Renewal replay (`renewal_test`, now with the returns first on every pair; confirmed on probe 48):** the 1,612 logged `Below(3)` draws (0x140F28759) fall on the right players for 1,607 of 1,607 draw-year rows (1,564 of 1,600 with the renewals first); renewed returnees get the game's wage 124 of 124 (0 of 8 before); all wages 5,133 of 5,153 (5,009 of 5,037). The other pairs without a draw log agree: probe 42 104 of 105 returnees, probe 47 124 of 124, probe 45 (1 January) 129 of 129.
- **Free-run renewal count (`ml_consistency` `sw_renewals_count`):** the model's own plan tiers now see the returnees in their owners' squads and renew about 2 % more players who did not move (probe 42: 3,334 to 3,387 against the game's 3,071; probes 47 and 48 likewise). Probe 42 crossed the 10 % band; the summer band is now 15 %, the same as the winter band, for the same known cause (the plan tiers over-renew by 8 to 12 %, entry 2026-11-14). This is a tolerance on a behaviour-model count, not a replay.
- **Audit (`private-reference/remediation/audit5_c1.tsv`, `state5_c1.tsv`; previous baseline `audit5_fix3b` kept):** everything up to the first switch is identical, generator included (state row `S2020.end`); from `S2021.build` on, all rows differ because the renewals' draws now fall on a different roster order. First switch: renewed 3,557 (3,556 before), deals 37 (34). Full suite 62 of 62.

### 2026-11-19: the 40-player limit counts a club's players on loan elsewhere (Tracks B and C)

What changed: the transfer model's limit of 40 (`kHardCap`, the buyer picks and the top-up) counts `Club::loaned_out`, the club's players held by another club on loan, with its squad; `transfer_world` fills it (each loanee once, at his owner) and a loan the model makes adds one to the seller's count. Found by C2's audit: a loan return took club 265 to 41 at the 2025 switch (hard invariant `club_roster_above_40`), because the model let an owner fill to 40 while a player was away.

- **Evidence (observed; the counting code is not read):** in 123 consecutive dump pairs (probes 42, 43, 47, 49 and 51) roster plus loaned out never exceeds 40; clubs with a roster of 36 to 39 whose roster plus loaned out was 40 signed nobody on 435 club-days, while clubs at the same rosters below that total signed on 65 of 4,023 (about 5 expected at that rate). Probes 42, 45, 47 and 48 around the switch steps: the same, and no club at 40 has a player out. The team record holds exactly 40 squad references (+0x14C to +0x28C, 8 bytes each; the count is +0x426 & 0x7F, the field `PlayerSearch_Index_Rebuild` 0x140F98FD0 bands at 20, 23, 25 and 35), so a return into a full squad would have no slot. `PlayerSearch_Quota_FillSquadTo18` 0x140FB2870 counts the club plan's squad vector; whether the plan holds the loanees is not read.
- **Tests:** `transfer_model_test` (clubs at 39 plus 1 out and at 40 sign nobody, a control at 39 with nobody out signs on 1 July, no deal lands on a club at the limit over the window, and squads plus loaned out grow by exactly the loans, free signings and regens; it fails with the old count) and `ml_deals_test` (after the July window no club is over 40 with its loanees, and after every loan has come back no squad is over 40).
- **Audit (`audit5_cap.tsv`, `state5_cap.tsv`, against `audit5_c1`, which is kept):** identical up to the 2021 switch, generator included; the first difference is `S2021.build` (the switch-day deals). Window flows stay within the spread of the earlier baselines (summer permanent moves 984 to 1,002 a season, loans 587 to 604, free signings 231 to 300); the October free pool runs 1,167, 1,192, 1,151, 1,105, 1,065 (C1: 1,163 to 1,217 then 1,146; fix3b: 1,162 to 1,056). No hard invariant breaks; `club_roster_below_18` (one club on 1 July 2021) is in all three baselines. Full suite 62 of 62.
- **Other paths that can still take a club over 40 (not changed here, reported):** the user's released youth go to their parent club at the switch with no room check; 6.6 % of the 2 January regens go to a random club, and the 72.3 % placed at their former club can find it refilled by the 1 January deals.

### 2026-11-19: correction C2, the 1 July build between the two parts of the switch (Track C)

What changed: `run_season_switch` is split into `run_season_switch_pre` (loan returns, renewals, the switch-day deals) and `run_season_switch_post` (retirement, development, leavers, the winter flag roll unchanged, fallback renewals, regens, finance). `run_until` runs pre, takes the build's team keys from the world at that point, runs `run_season_build`, then post; `run_season_switch` keeps both parts without a build for the callers that build nothing. The driver's stages are now SeasonEnd, BeforeBuild, AfterBuild, SwitchDone, SeasonStart (AfterSwitch is gone); the audit, `season_run_test`'s reference loop, `ml_season_test`, `ml_consistency` and `pes_host --ml-days` follow the same order. No algorithm changed.

- **Evidence for the order (confirmed):** probe 48's draw log has the renewals at draw 636, the CPU agents' transfer work to 148,662, the build from 148,665, the development from 161,406 and the retiree reset after it (entry above). The post part reads club membership again after the deals: `season_development_test` already develops the user's players who left before the development.
- **D4, the build's keys (confirmed by the cup lists, separately from the draw log):** probe 48's build replayed from the logged state at draw 148,665 with the game's lists of regs 2, 5 and 91 reproduces the 14 cup lists 14 of 14 only with the squads after the step's moves and the ratings before the development (`ml_consistency` `build_time_keys`). Squads before the switch: 10 of 14; with only the loan returns applied: 13 of 14 (club 5356 needs its 3 incoming transfers); squads and ratings after the step: 2 of 14.
- **Finance stays last:** `switch_finance` takes the generator by value, so its two draws never moved the main stream, and its evidence is the squad the switch leaves (probes 42 and 48). Its draws' place in the game (148,663 and 148,664) is therefore not modelled.
- **Replays:** probe 48 build with the game's lists 9,927 of 9,927 records; cups 14 of 14, leagues 15 of 15; the development, regen and renewal replays are separate tests and pass. The integrated switch cannot run from the game's generator state: the model's own build lists (reg 2) differ, and the model's leave-as-free `Below(1000)` draws (not the game's) come before the development.
